Title: How Trump could interfere in US midterm elections
Article:
WASHINGTON: State officials who run US elections are bracing for further intervention by President Donald Trump's administration in next week's midterms, fearing federal authorities could disrupt voting, challenge ballot counts or try to block unfavourable results.
Trump, whose Republicans face an uphill battle to retain control of Congress, has repeatedly questioned the integrity of US elections and urged his party to "nationalise" voting in at least 15 places.
The White House says it is protecting election security, and many of the feared scenarios remain hypothetical. The US Constitution gives the president no direct role in running elections, and federal courts have so far rebuffed the administration's main legal challenges.
Here are the key potential flashpoints:
Before election day
Voter eligibility: The Justice Department has sued 30 states and the District of Columbia to obtain their voter registration lists, saying it needs them to identify non-citizens. It has lost more than two dozen of those cases.
It has also demanded that ballots be set aside from about 20,000 people in California and more than 400 in Washington state whom it suspects are non-citizens.
A federal judge rejected the California request on Wednesday, saying it would wreak havoc on an election already under way. Washington state has also refused the demand.
Studies have repeatedly found non-citizen voting to be exceptionally rare.
Pressure on officials: The Justice Department has warned election officials in every state that they could face prosecution if they knowingly allow non-citizens to vote.
And Trump on Monday offered US$1 million for information leading to a voter fraud conviction, without giving details.
[[nid:1566733]]
At polling stations
Federal monitors: The Justice Department plans to send around 1,000 election monitors to all 50 states — its largest deployment ever.
Monitoring is a decades-old practice, but Democrats and voting rights groups fear monitors could intimidate voters. The department says they will be unarmed, barred from interfering with voting and drawn from neither the FBI nor Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).
Immigration agents and troops: Advocates fear ICE operations near polling stations could deter voters in immigrant communities.
The administration says it is not planning operations targeting polling places, although Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin has said ICE agents could serve warrants there.
Trump has declined to rule out declaring a national emergency or invoking the Insurrection Act, which allows the president to deploy troops at home.
A Civil War-era law bars troops and armed federal agents from polling places, and legal experts say an emergency declaration would not give the president power over elections.
Counting the votes
Seizing election materials: Federal agents could seek warrants or subpoenas for ballots, voting machines or records — potentially disrupting the count.
In January, the FBI seized ballots and other 2020 election records in Fulton County, Georgia, a focus of Trump's false claims that he won that year.
Election officials warn that similar action during an active count could undermine safeguards for tracking how ballots are handled.
Challenging the count: Trump could allege fraud involving mail-in ballots, voting machines or votes counted after election night, fuelling demands for recounts or attempts to halt counting.
But the US Supreme Court ruled in June that states may count mail ballots postmarked by election day that arrive afterwards, and courts can intervene against unlawful disruption.
[[nid:1566731]]
After election day
Blocking certification: The Justice Department has sued Alaska to delay certification of its Senate race if Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan narrowly loses to Democrat Mary Peltola, citing a second candidate named Dan Sullivan who it says is trying to confuse voters — a claim he denies.
Trump said he ordered the lawsuit.
Experts say federal law does not allow the department to block certification, which courts can compel officials to carry out.
Challenging Democratic victories: Trump could pressure state officials to dispute results, as he did after losing the 2020 election.
Experts warn unresolved disputes could also delay the swearing-in of newly elected lawmakers in January.
But courts have repeatedly upheld states' authority over elections, and Democrats and voting rights groups have assembled legal teams to fight any interference.

Title: GIIB shares extend losses amid heavy selling
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Shares in GIIB Holdings Bhd continued to slide on Friday, falling as much as 55.56 per cent in early trade, a day after a sharp decline prompted an unusual market activity (UMA) query from Bursa Malaysia Securities Bhd.
The rubber compounds manufacturer's shares fell to a morning low of 24 sen before recovering to 33 sen as at 9.53am, still down 21 sen or 38.89 per cent from Thursday's close of 54 sen.
The stock opened marginally higher at 54.5 sen before reversing course. It was the second most actively traded counter on Bursa Malaysia, with 46.18 million shares changing hands.
On Thursday, the stock plunged 23.94 per cent from 71 sen to 54 sen, wiping RM140.5 million off its market capitalisation, which fell to RM446.2 million from RM586.7 million.
The company had yet to respond to Bursa's query as at press time.
The sell-off marks a sharp reversal for GIIB, whose shares had surged more than ninefold from around eight sen earlier this year to a high of 74 sen on Oct 23.
At 33 sen, the stock was down 41 sen, or 55.41 per cent, from that peak. It remained more than 300 per cent higher year to date.
GIIB had previously received two UMA queries following unusual movements in its share price in late April.
In its earlier responses, the company cited its proposed diversification into the healthcare sector and said it was complying with Bursa Malaysia's listing requirements.
Businessman Datuk Ng Meng Kee is a substantial shareholder of GIIB, holding a 7.17 per cent direct stake and a 7.87 per cent indirect interest through Mega Fortris Global Pte Ltd and Mega Fortris Capital Ltd.
Ng is also the non-independent non-executive chairman of Mega Fortris Bhd, whose shares fell 20.58 per cent to RM2.74 on Thursday from RM3.45.
Mega Fortris extended its losses on Friday, falling as much as 19.34 per cent, or 53 sen, to RM2.21 after opening 9.49 per cent higher at RM3.

Title: Netanyahu bloc finishes ahead in Israel vote, but well short of majority
Article:
JERUSALEM: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's camp finished ahead of the opposition but remained well short of a majority, final results from Israel's general election showed on Friday, setting the stage for tough coalition talks or potentially another vote.
Netanyahu's coalition of right-wing and far-right parties won 53 of the Knesset's 120 seats, with his Likud party remaining the largest faction with 27 seats.
The opposition bloc, led by centrist Gadi Eisenkot, secured 48 seats.
The results from the Central Elections Committee also cemented the emergence of the Arab party groupings Raam and the Joint List as potential kingmakers, with the two winning a combined 19 seats.
The fragmented outcome sets the stage for difficult negotiations to form a government, which could last weeks, with no single bloc able to reach the 61-seat threshold needed. The prospect of another election remains if talks fail.
The final tally came after Netanyahu's camp spent Thursday amplifying unproven allegations that Arab-Israeli groups had received foreign funding to influence the vote, accusations rejected by both Arab-majority lists and Qatar.
Israel's Shin Bet domestic security service said it was investigating suspected irregularities but stressed that the probe was not intended to "cast aspersions or place blame on an entire sector that went out to vote in a democratic and lawful manner".
The electoral commission also sought to calm tensions, with its acting director general Dean Livne saying any suggestion of widespread issues was "entirely groundless".
Political earthquake
The controversy centred on allegations that Raam received money from Qatar, the energy-rich Gulf powerbroker that has channels to Hamas, to finance vote-buying operations.
"The Raamgate scandal is a political earthquake. Israel's elections have been stolen!" Netanyahu's Likud party said on Thursday.
Raam leader Mansour Abbas denied any wrongdoing and welcomed an investigation, while the Joint List accused Netanyahu and his allies of conducting a "campaign of incitement" out of fear of Arab voters' growing political influence.
[[nid:1566721]]
Government officials have so far provided no evidence to back the allegations.
Opposition figures accused Netanyahu of attempting to undermine confidence in the results after failing to secure a governing majority.
"He is trying to challenge the election results," left-wing candidate Yair Golan said.
Eisenkot said he had been briefed by the Shin Bet and the election committee, adding that it was "too early to understand what happened, and whether anything happened at all".
But he continued: "It's already clear that Likud and Netanyahu have embarked on a coordinated, organised campaign seeking to delegitimise the results of the election."
Netanyahu himself has long been under a cloud of allegations related to Qatar after two of his aides were arrested last year for allegedly receiving payments from the Gulf state.
Qatar called the latest accusations "ridiculous and dangerous".
Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister, for years tacitly supported Qatar funding Hamas in Gaza, hoping to preserve stability, but that approach collapsed on Oct 7, 2023.
Kingmakers under pressure
Yousef Jabareen, head of the Joint List, told AFP that he was willing to cooperate with the opposition to bring down Netanyahu but without joining it in a government.
Netanyahu had tried during the voting to raise allegations of fraud, saying that Arab parties had been caught with envelopes of cash, and Likud peddled the accusations throughout Thursday.
Police said they had arrested three suspects, but the election commission called it an isolated local case.

Title: Teen rallies take to the streets across Italy
Article:
ROME: School and university students are set to rally in several Italian cities on Friday to call for more funding for schools and support for housing, with security forces preparing for possible clashes.
Students have been protesting for weeks, setting up tent camps and occupying schools to make their demands heard, mirroring similar movements across the border in France.
The Italian protests have taken place alongside those by truck drivers and farmers over rising fuel prices and the cost of living, as well as increased defence spending.
"On Friday, we expect a massive mobilisation of students, who will block and empty schools," Laura Teresi, 18, from Rome's Cavour high school and a spokesperson for the OSA student movement, told AFP.
"We will take to the streets to denounce the rearmament policies of (Prime Minister Giorgia) Meloni's government and the rising cost of living, which is weighing ever more heavily on families, workers and students," she added.
The students will also protest against the "endless budget cuts to teaching", Teresi said.
Officials are worried about a repeat of the violence on Oct 17 and 18 in Milan, the country's economic capital, where groups of young people set cars on fire and looted shops.
'Malaise'
The radical left USB union has called for a general strike on Friday.
"The broader Italian and European context is marked by a crisis and a social, economic and cultural malaise affecting different segments of society and different regions," said Rosario Forlenza, professor of contemporary history and political anthropology at Rome's Luiss University.
"The younger generation (is)... a generation that is underrepresented politically, that sees political leaders' attention focused elsewhere and therefore lives in a situation of precarity, social distress and even a lack of a future," Forlenza said.
In response to the youth protests, Meloni's hard-right government has eased rules on detaining minors and toughened laws on public gatherings.
The government also agreed last week on a 175.2-million-euro (US$195 million) aid package for truck drivers, farmers and fishermen hit by soaring fuel prices linked to the war in the Middle East.
Measures in favour of young people and families are also planned in the draft 2027 budget currently being discussed among the various governing parties, including an annual bonus of 2,500 euros for workers under 30.
"I hope this can provide answers for young people in general... who feel that the state doesn't care about them," Meloni said at a press conference on Wednesday, stressing that these measures were "not for those who smash windows".
Psychologist and psychotherapist Matteo Lancini said part of the problem was schools themselves because they were "totally disconnected" from young people's needs.
"What we need are schools that change radically, schools that are not designed around adults' pension systems," Lancini said at a meeting with the foreign press in Rome.
Instead, "everyone eases their conscience by saying it's social media's fault", he said.

Title: Penang tops global ranking for budget-friendly digital nomad living
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Penang has been ranked the world's most budget-friendly city for digital nomads in a new international study covering 26 cities across 15 countries.
The study, conducted by digital marketing agency Click Intelligence and featured in Moneywise in October, placed Penang first with an overall score of 0.78.
Busan in South Korea came second, followed by Kuala Lumpur in third place. Fukuoka and Seoul, also in South Korea, took fourth and fifth positions respectively.
The remaining cities in the top 10 were Tartu in Estonia, Chiang Mai in Thailand, Valencia in Spain, Osaka in Japan and Brno in the Czech Republic.
A digital nomad is a location-independent professional who uses the internet and digital technology to work remotely while travelling.
The study estimated Penang's monthly living cost, including rent, at €850 (about RM3,860). It highlighted the city's affordability, internet connectivity, safety and access to Malaysia's DE Rantau Nomad Pass.
The DE Rantau Nomad Pass is a programme for eligible remote workers, allowing them to live in Malaysia for 12 months, with an option to renew.
Click Intelligence co-founder and director James Owen said language is rarely a barrier, as English is widely spoken across the island.
He also said Malaysia is generally considered a safe place to live.
Penang Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai said the international recognition reflected the state's growing appeal as a destination for digital nomads and international visitors.
"Penang offers more than affordable living.
"Our Unesco World Heritage status, rich multicultural heritage, world-famous food, vibrant arts and creative scene, as well as beautiful natural attractions, make the state an attractive place to live, work and explore," he said.
Wong said the recognition also reinforced the state's efforts to strengthen its tourism industry and creative economy.
"Penang has the lifestyle, culture and opportunities that international visitors and digital nomads are looking for," he added.

Title: BTH: Sugar Babies: Where does consent end and exploitation begin? [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sugar baby arrangements do not automatically constitute criminal conduct, but those involving coercion, exploitation or sexual services may cross legal boundaries, a criminologist has warned.
Speaking on this week's Beyond the Headlines, criminologist Dr Haezreena Begum Abdul Hamid said authorities must assess the circumstances of each case, as financial assistance between consenting adults does not, by itself, amount to solicitation or prostitution.
She said describing payments as gifts or allowances did not automatically place such arrangements outside the law, adding that the nature of the exchange and the conduct involved were crucial in determining whether an offence had occurred.
Haezreena also warned that financial dependence could become a means of control, with seemingly consensual relationships escalating into manipulation, pressure to engage in unwanted sexual activities, blackmail or extortion.
Other warning signs include grooming, emotional manipulation and isolation, as well as threats to expose private messages or photographs when one party attempts to end the relationship.
She said universities should strengthen financial assistance, counselling services and confidential reporting mechanisms to help vulnerable students seek support without fear of humiliation or disciplinary action.
She added that policymakers and relevant agencies needed better evidence on the extent of exploitation linked to such arrangements to develop targeted prevention measures and ensure accountability.
Rather than treating all transactional relationships as exploitative, she said, efforts should focus on identifying coercion and abuse while ensuring those affected could access help.
More in the latest episode of NST's Beyond the Headlines on NST Online's YouTube channel.

Title: Bursa Malaysia slips after higher opening
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia slipped into negative territory on Friday after opening slightly higher, tracking weaker overnight sentiment on Wall Street amid disappointing technology earnings.
At 9.13 am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) eased 0.66 of a point, or 0.04 per cent, to 1,610.50 from Thursday's close of 1,611.16.
The benchmark index had opened 0.70 of a point higher at 1,611.86.
Across the broader market, losers outnumbered gainers 265 to 107, while 265 counters were unchanged, 2,143 remained untraded and 66 were suspended.
Turnover stood at 291.30 million units worth RM95.01 million.
Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said Wall Street closed mostly lower following weaker earnings from US technology giant Alphabet Inc, reigniting concerns over the substantial capital expenditure required for artificial intelligence (AI) investments.
"On the home front, we believe the benchmark index remains in consolidation mode, with fundamentally sound blue chips offering selective opportunities following the recent correction.
"Hence, for today, we envisage the benchmark index hovering within the 1,600-1,620 range," he told Bernama.
Among heavyweight stocks, Maybank rose two sen to RM10.02, while CIMB gained seven sen to RM6.96 and IHH Healthcare added four sen to RM7.89. Public Bank shed one sen to RM4.72, while Tenaga Nasional was unchanged at RM13.30.
In active trade, Zetrix AI and JAKS Resources shed one sen each to seven sen and 14 sen, respectively. GIIB Holdings fell 10.5 sen to 43.5 sen, while Ni Hsin and EWI Capital gained one sen each to 38 sen and 14.5 sen, respectively.
Country View topped the gainers, rising 14 sen to RM2.85, followed by Kein Hing, which added six sen to RM1.08. Genting Plantations gained five sen to RM5.10, while Lianson Fleet rose four sen to RM1.52.
Among the top losers, Malaysian Pacific Industries fell 60 sen to RM40.90, while UWC Bhd shed 20 sen to RM7.44. MN Holdings declined 12 sen to RM3.83, while Pentamaster Corporation lost nine sen to RM5.80.
On the index board, the FBM Emas Index fell 17.00 points to 12,038.89, while the FBM Top 100 Index shed 15.29 points to 11,835.67. The FBM Mid 70 Index declined 66.17 points to 17,417.95, the FBM Emas Shariah Index lost 32.73 points to 12,051.55, and the FBM ACE Index slipped 32.61 points to 5,414.55.
Sector-wise, the Energy Index increased 0.28 of a point to 844.64, the Financial Services Index jumped 18.69 points to 18,556.63, while the Plantation Index added 18.44 points to 8,655.34. The Industrial Products and Services Index edged down 0.36 of a point to 177.03.

Title: Indonesian drought could lift Malaysian planters
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian plantation companies could benefit from firmer crude palm oil (CPO) prices in 2027 as worsening drought conditions in Indonesia threaten to tighten regional supply.
CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd said the latest production outlook from Wilmar International Ltd had reinforced concerns over drought-related supply disruptions extending into next year.
Singapore-listed Wilmar is one of the world's largest oil palm plantation groups.
As at end-2025, the group had 234,334 hectares of planted oil palm estates, with about 66 per cent in Indonesia and another 25 per cent in East Malaysia.
The agribusiness group now expects fresh fruit bunch (FFB) production at its Indonesian estates to decline this year, reversing its earlier forecast of slight growth.
The revised outlook reflects worse-than-expected drought conditions in South Sumatra and parts of Kalimantan.
"Wilmar's weaker Indonesian palm oil output outlook reinforces concerns about drought-related supply risks extending into 2027, supporting our constructive crude palm oil view," CIMB Securities said.
The research firm said tighter supply could benefit Malaysian plantation companies with estates in Malaysia, although those with significant Indonesian exposure could also face weaker FFB yields next year.
CIMB Securities maintained its "Overweight" rating on the plantation sector, with Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd (KLK), SD Guthrie Bhd and IOI Corporation Bhd among its preferred picks.
It maintained "Buy" calls on all three companies, with target prices of RM24.32 for KLK, RM6.52 for SD Guthrie and RM5.03 for IOI Corporation.
However, the research firm cautioned that near-term CPO price gains could be limited by elevated Malaysian palm oil inventories, weak consumption and the possibility of improved sunflower oil supply from the Black Sea region.
It said a meaningful recovery in palm oil demand from Chinese buyers would depend on a sustained price discount against soybean oil.

Title: Binance's possible hack triggers US$3 billion freeze in crypto assets
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, said on Thursday it had frozen US$3 billion in crypto assets as it investigated a potential security breach, with stablecoin issuers Circle and Tether also freezing related assets.
"Binance will cover all hacking losses," Binance co-founder Yi He said, without providing further details about the incident.
The market impact of the potential hack, which could be the largest-ever cryptocurrency heist, according to analytics firm Chainalysis, was felt immediately in early Asian trading on Friday.
Bitcoin fell about 2 per cent to a six-week low of US$77,646, while ether dropped around 2 per cent to a two-month low of US$2,238.76.
BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, fell more than 8 per cent over the past 24 hours to US$694, according to market aggregator CoinGecko.
Crypto exchange Coinbase Global fell 4.8 per cent, while shares of bitcoin buyer Strategy dropped nearly 6 per cent in extended US trading.
Binance said the amount frozen could increase as it worked with law enforcement agencies, token issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and other industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets.
Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao, who no longer runs the company, said in a post on X that the incident "looked like a hack".
Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has more than 335 million registered users globally and held about US$160 billion in assets under custody, according to its 2024 annual report.
BINANCE HAS SECURE ASSET FUND
Binance operates a secure asset fund for users, according to its website. The reserve is held entirely in bitcoin and is intended to protect user assets in the event of security breaches.
"It's becoming very hard to counter hacks as AI can find vulnerabilities faster than you can fix them," said Bernardo Brites, chief executive officer of Trace Finance, a payments and stablecoin infrastructure company.
"My view is that users will move away from smaller and medium-sized exchanges, (it is) becoming too risky to park your money somewhere that couldn't cover a hack of meaningful size."
Tether said it had frozen nearly US$1.57 billion in assets linked to the incident, while Circle froze more than US$800 million.
Binance said it was conducting security checks and would resume withdrawals once the issue was fully resolved. It added that user funds remained safe and its teams were reviewing the incident.
The exchange also temporarily suspended trading on its Binance Alpha platform as a precaution.
World Liberty Financial, a cryptocurrency company linked to US President Donald Trump and his family, said on Thursday it had worked with cryptocurrency custodian BitGo to freeze funds stolen in what it described as a Binance hack.
Yi said US$27 million in stablecoins and about US$2 million worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen.
Cryptocurrency firm Ripple also froze roughly US$200 million in funds, Yi said.
Jack McDonald, senior vice-president of stablecoins at Ripple, said the company was closely monitoring reports of a potential exploit involving Binance and was freezing affected funds while coordinating with relevant parties.
INCIDENT ADDS TO STRING OF CRYPTO THEFTS
Miguel Morel, chief executive officer of blockchain intelligence firm Arkham, said data indicated that billions of dollars appeared to have been stolen from Binance by an unknown actor, although the exact cause had not been confirmed.
Morel said the incident began at around 4.30pm EDT (2030 GMT) and appeared to be ongoing.
The incident adds to a string of cryptocurrency thefts. Attackers stole US$2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks last year, according to researchers at TRM Labs.
In September, cryptocurrency exchange Bitget said about US$350 million in crypto assets had been stolen from its platform, underscoring the industry's vulnerability to hackers.
Authorities have warned that organised crime groups are increasingly using cryptocurrencies to move funds across borders outside the traditional financial system.
Binance.US, a separate cryptocurrency exchange, said it was not affected by the security incident.
Coinbase said it was also unaffected and was monitoring the situation.
In an unrelated incident earlier on Thursday, prediction market operator Polymarket temporarily halted trading following a security incident involving a third-party provider. It later resumed trading and said it would fully reimburse affected traders.

Title: Norhizam unfazed by 'pig-shooting assemblyman' label
Article:
MELAKA: Former Pengkalan Batu assemblyman Datuk Norhizam Hassan Baktee is unfazed by the nicknames he earned during his previous tenure, including "YB Beliau" and the "pig-shooting assemblyman", as he prepares to return to public service.
The 60-year-old Bersatu candidate said the labels were simply part of his experience as a people's representative, particularly his willingness to go to the ground and address residents' problems.
He said when elected in 2018, he had always strived to serve the community to the best of his ability, recognising that the mandate and opportunity came from the people.
"Look at the labels I received. Which assemblyman would dare to go out and shoot wild boars? I was even called a pig, but to me, it was just a nickname.
"An elected representative must be courageous and work with sincerity to solve the people's problems. That was what I did before, and I intend to do even better this time," he said.
He was speaking after Bersatu's candidate announcement at the party's main operations room at Baitul Tariq in Klebang last night.
Norhizam, who is also Bersatu Hang Tuah Jaya deputy division chief, said that despite turning 60, he wanted to focus on residents' basic needs, particularly flash floods caused by drainage and clogged drains, which he claimed had yet to be comprehensively addressed.
He also highlighted road conditions, education and the need to help small entrepreneurs obtain business licences and suitable premises.
He pledged to push for fairer opportunities for small G1 and G2-class contractors through open tenders, instead of large-scale concession-based project awards that make it difficult for smaller contractors to secure work.
"Small contractors are struggling to earn a living, and we will do our best to help them secure suitable work opportunities," he said.
On the contest for the seat, the former Melaka state executive councillor for agriculture, entrepreneur development, cooperatives and agro-based industries said his previous experience as the area's assemblyman and ties with residents would help him connect with voters.
He said he was prepared to sacrifice sleep, having previously managed with only about three hours a night to focus on serving the public.
"People say I am already 60, but my spirit is still going strong," he said.
Norhizam won the Pengkalan Batu seat in the 2018 14th General Election (GE14) under the DAP ticket with 9,227 votes.
After leaving DAP, he contested as an independent candidate in the 2021 Melaka election but lost to Barisan Nasional's Datuk Kalsom Noordin, securing 1,218 votes.

Title: Mi Technovation poised for strong year-end finish
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Mi Technovation Bhd is poised for stronger earnings in the final quarter of 2026 after its nine-month performance exceeded market expectations.
The stronger-than-expected results prompted Public Investment Bank Bhd (PublicInvest) to raise its earnings forecasts for the semiconductor equipment and materials manufacturer.
PublicInvest said the group's core net profit surged 73 per cent year-on-year to RM152 million in the first nine months of the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026 (FY26).
The earnings accounted for 78.4 per cent of the research firm's full-year forecast and 90 per cent of consensus estimates.
Following the results, PublicInvest raised its FY26 to FY28 earnings forecasts by about 10 per cent and maintained its "Outperform" call, with a higher target price of RM9.45.
The research firm expects earnings momentum to continue into the fourth quarter, supported by stronger demand for semiconductor materials and a recovery in equipment deliveries.
Mi Technovation's semiconductor materials business remained its main earnings contributor, generating more than RM100 million in earnings during the nine-month period.
The division is expected to gain further momentum in the fourth quarter, driven by demand from high-performance computing and memory customers, alongside steady orders from the mobility and wearables segment.
Meanwhile, its semiconductor equipment business is expected to record double-digit revenue growth for the full year despite a 2.2 per cent decline in the first nine months, implying a substantial recovery in fourth-quarter deliveries.
For the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, Mi Technovation's core net profit jumped 82.2 per cent to RM66.5 million from a year earlier, supported by stronger contributions from its semiconductor materials business.
Revenue grew 30 per cent year-on-year, driven mainly by semiconductor materials sales, which doubled to RM154 million.
The increase was supported by stronger demand for solder spheres from the mobility and wearables segment, sustained orders from high-performance computing and memory customers, and a gradual recovery in the automotive and renewable energy segments.
The semiconductor materials division's earnings tripled to RM55.1 million from RM18 million a year earlier.
PublicInvest attributed the improvement to higher capacity utilisation of more than 85 per cent at its Tainan plant in Taiwan and stronger sales of higher-margin patented solder spheres.
Better performance at its Ningbo plant in China also contributed to the growth.
The division recorded a net profit margin of 28.1 per cent for the first nine months of FY26.
In contrast, revenue from the semiconductor equipment business fell 18.7 per cent year-on-year to RM100.4 million in the third quarter, likely due to lower equipment deliveries, although the average selling price per machine increased.
PublicInvest expects deliveries of Mi Series die-sorting and smart-binning equipment, as well as Si Series test handlers, to pick up in the fourth quarter.
Meanwhile, Mi Technovation's newer semiconductor technologies and vehicle technologies businesses remained loss-making, recording combined losses of RM24.5 million in the first nine months.
PublicInvest said commercial production of the group's Vanda 1 power management chip had been delayed until the third quarter of 2027 due to prolonged wafer fabrication lead times.
Development of Vanda 2, however, remained on track.
The group's electric powertrain systems business was also ramping up operations, with commercialisation expected to support significant growth in 2027.

Title: Azalina: Govt open to releasing full report on Azam Baki's shareholding
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government is open to making public the full report of a special committee that investigated allegations of share ownership involving former Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief commissioner Tan Sri Azam Baki, subject to legal considerations.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said disclosure would be considered if necessary.
She said any decision must take into account existing legal provisions, particularly those governing personal data protection, the confidentiality of investigation documents, asset declaration records and the interests of relevant parties.
"Any announcement will be made by the Chief Secretary to the Government's Office, as stated in its March 31 media statement, should there be any official developments or decisions that warrant public disclosure.
"The issue of ownership and asset declarations, including Azam's shareholding, has been examined by the Special Investigation Committee established on Feb 13. The same question was also raised on June 25.
"The committee has completed its investigation independently, transparently and professionally, and its findings have been presented to the Cabinet," she said in a written parliamentary reply published on the parliament website today.
She was responding to Khoo Poay Tiong (PH-Kota Melaka), who asked about the committee's findings on allegations concerning Azam's shareholding, any action to be taken against him and whether the government was prepared to make the report public.

Title: Amazon burns cash, Intel flags weak PC demand as AI boom's costs ripple across markets
Article:
NEW YORK: Wall Street's concerns over the cost of the artificial intelligence (AI) boom escalated after the market closed on Thursday, as results from Amazon and Intel showed that the infrastructure race was not only straining the technology industry but also affecting consumers.
Surging data centre spending, highlighted by Amazon's massive cash burn, has turned once debt-light technology giants into major borrowers, while price increases are squeezing global demand for devices such as smartphones and personal computers (PCs).
Amazon forecast holiday-quarter sales below Wall Street expectations, potentially signalling growing pressure on consumers as inflation picks up. This also affected Intel's PC business, as a memory chip shortage drove up its costs.
The AI spending spree is also eating into the once-enviable cash flows of major technology companies. Alphabet and Meta both burned cash in the September quarter, while Microsoft, the only exception, joined their borrowing spree with a US$25 billion debt sale on Thursday.
The technology giants have deep pockets to sustain their spending, but investors have grown increasingly wary of smaller AI cloud firms borrowing heavily to meet enormous order backlogs.
Amazon's shares fell 7 per cent in after-hours trading, accompanied by losses of between 5.8 and 6.7 per cent in AI cloud stocks CoreWeave, Nebius and Iren. Alphabet, which closed regular trading nearly 13 per cent lower, fell another 1.5 per cent after hours.
The semiconductor index also fell after the market closed after Intel cited "near-term headwinds across the PC industry". The index had already dropped 1.4 per cent during the regular session following Alphabet's disappointing earnings report.
Shares of PC makers HP and Dell fell 8 per cent and 6.8 per cent, respectively.
"The revenues missed due to lower PC demand and forward guidance also disappointed. As Google learned today, earnings matter," said Kim Caughey Forrest, founder and chief investment officer at Bokeh Capital Partners LLC.
Alphabet, Google's parent company, fell 13 per cent on Thursday.
INTEL FACTORY SHUTDOWN
Intel, whose shares fell 18 per cent, also said a factory explosion in Israel had caused a two-week shutdown and would cost it about US$600 million in lost revenue over two quarters.
"Overall semiconductor weakness after hours is primarily a function of Intel guide and negative sentiment spillover," said Michael James, equity sales trader at Rosenblatt Securities.
Some analysts said Intel's problems in the PC sector, an area of technology that does not attract the same scrutiny on Wall Street as the AI buildout, did not necessarily point to major problems for other chipmakers with greater exposure to AI.
Nevertheless, investors in the less-active after-hours market appeared to react first and ask questions later. AMD fell 4 per cent and Broadcom declined 2 per cent.
Among the biggest losers in the volatile session was the Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull ETF, which offers investors three times the daily performance of the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX), and fell 9 per cent.
The SOX has been one of 2026's standout performers, rising more than 60 per cent as shortages of chips and equipment needed for the AI buildout drove up prices and profits at companies ranging from Nvidia and memory chipmaker Micron to Marvell Technology.
However, the momentum of the trade has been tested over the past month by tighter financing conditions. This has kept some anticipated initial public offerings (IPOs) on the sidelines and put some highly leveraged AI infrastructure firms under pressure.
The SOX has declined 13 per cent since hitting its recent high in October and is down 21 per cent from its all-time high in June.
"I think Intel was seen as this unicorn within the tech sector because it was seen as being weaker compared to Nvidia and AMD," said Jake Dollarhide, chief executive officer of Longbow Asset Management in Tulsa, Oklahoma.
"It just had this miraculous rise, and you got a lot of retail money into it, and some of that money is easy come, easy go."

Title: Ministry targets year-end rollout of revised abandoned vehicle guidelines
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Housing and Local Government Ministry is studying the need to improve existing legal provisions to address the issue of abandoned vehicles.
Its minister, Nga Kor Ming, said the joint initiative with the Transport Ministry aims to clarify powers and expedite enforcement and disposal processes while safeguarding the rights of vehicle owners.
The approach, he said, aims to shift the management of abandoned vehicles from a purely enforcement model to a comprehensive solution balancing legal authority, public rights, and owners' social responsibility.
"The ministry, in cooperation with the Transport Ministry, is also improving approaches through the use of various legal instruments that can be considered.
"This includes the Road Transport Act 1987, as well as introducing a more systematic voluntary disposal method to encourage owners to legally dispose of obsolete vehicles.
"The ministry is also improving the Guidelines for the Management of Abandoned Vehicles in Local Authority Operational Areas introduced in 2020.
"This aims to streamline procedures for tracking, removing, storing, and disposing of abandoned vehicles based on available powers under relevant laws, including the Street, Drainage and Building Act 1974," he said in a written reply published on the Parliament portal today.
He was responding to a question from Jimmy Puah (PH-Tebrau) on the ministry's plans to draft or amend existing laws to tackle abandoned vehicles nationwide.
Nga said the new guidelines are expected to be implemented by local authorities in the peninsula before the end of this year, while implementation in Sabah and Sarawak will be coordinated with the respective authorities according to applicable legal frameworks.
"The government stresses that the approach to managing abandoned vehicles is not merely issuing guidelines, but involves a comprehensive action framework based on good governance, field evidence, inter-agency coordination, and practical work process improvements for local authorities to implement.
"The government is confident that with the support of all parties, including the Transport Ministry and the police, the issue of abandoned vehicles can be addressed more effectively and holistically," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Gold prices edge lower as US inflation data reinforces Fed outlook
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Gold prices eased in early Asian trade on Friday after falling more than one per cent in the previous session, as persistent US inflation fuelled expectations of further Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hikes, weighing on bullion.
FUNDAMENTALS
Spot gold fell 0.4 per cent to US$4,006.06 an ounce by 0036 GMT, while US gold futures for December delivery dropped 0.3 per cent to US$4,018.50.
Bullion was headed for a modest weekly gain but remained on track for a second consecutive monthly decline.
US inflation accelerated in September as consumers paid more for petrol and other goods, supporting economists' expectations of a Fed interest rate increase in December.
Traders are now pricing in about a 75 per cent chance of a rate hike in December, according to the CME FedWatch Tool.
Higher interest rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion, reducing its appeal to investors.
The European Central Bank (ECB) left interest rates unchanged in a widely anticipated move on Thursday but clearly signalled another hike in December, warning that high and rising energy costs were fuelling inflation risks.
ECB president Christine Lagarde will step down from her role on Feb 7, the central bank said.
Annual core inflation in Japan's capital exceeded the central bank's two per cent target by a wide margin in October, data showed on Friday, highlighting mounting price pressures and strengthening the case for further interest rate hikes.
The London Metal Exchange is seeking to turn metal held in its Hong Kong warehouses into digital assets that can be used for financing, a move linked to the territory's five-year plan to expand its commodities hub, three people familiar with the matter said.
Spot silver fell one per cent to US$51.87 an ounce, platinum was steady at US$1,488.00, while palladium declined 0.5 per cent to US$1,000.75.
All three metals were headed for weekly and monthly declines.

Title: Iran says four tankers on fire after hitting mines in Hormuz
Article:
TEHERAN: Four tankers caught fire after hitting mines while attempting to navigate the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's armed forces said on Thursday, a day after the US military said it had cleared key routes through the waterway.
"Over the past 24 hours, three violating oil tankers exploded and caught fire after striking mines while attempting to pass through the unauthorised southern route of the Strait of Hormuz," Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) said in a statement.
Later on Thursday, Iran's army reported that another tanker had caught fire east of the strait after hitting mines while "operating in a restricted and dangerous area".
The initial three vessels had "switched off all their radar and navigation systems" and disregarded warnings from the IRGC navy, the statement said.
It was not immediately clear when the incidents occurred or which flags the tankers were flying.
British maritime agency UKMTO, meanwhile, said late on Thursday that it had received a report of a vessel on fire about 25 nautical miles (46km) northeast of Khasab, Oman, in the Strait of Hormuz.
Earlier, UKMTO reported two other incidents in the area: a dhow that caught fire and sank following a maritime security incident, and a tanker struck by an unknown projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz.
In recent weeks, Iran has reported multiple vessels striking sea mines, prompting US Central Command (Centcom), which oversees military operations in the region, to reaffirm on social media its claim that all mines in "primary transit routes" had been cleared.
On Thursday, Hossein Mohebi, the IRGC spokesman, challenged the claim, saying on X: "Prove your Hormuz mine-clearing claim with independent evidence, not statements!"
Since the outbreak of the war on Feb 28, Iran has severely restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.
The United States has responded by imposing a blockade on Iranian ports and helping tankers travel through the strait. On Sunday, Centcom said it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer.
Iran considers ships using the southern corridor near the Omani coast unauthorised.
In their statement on Thursday, the Guards said "the unauthorised route through the Strait of Hormuz is mined, and that vessel owners and crews are responsible for transiting these routes and should not pay attention to Centcom's delusions on social media".
The IRGC also said it had captured a US reconnaissance drone in a separate statement.
"The IRGC Navy announced that its electronic warfare unit had successfully captured a US MQM-170 drone during an offensive operation in the western Strait of Hormuz," the statement said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kuala Pilah floods displace 38, including nine senior citizens
Article:
KUALA PILAH: A temporary flood relief centre was opened at Sekolah Kebangsaan Undang Johol last night after two areas were hit by floods.
The centre opened at 10.25pm to house 38 victims from 17 families from Rumah Rakyat Kuala Johol and Kampung Padang Jual, Johol.
A Kuala Pilah Social Welfare Department spokesman said the centre was opened after the Johol state constituency headman reported rising floodwaters that had yet to recede in both locations.
Following that, the evacuation order was issued to ensure the safety of all victims.
The spokesman said as of 4am today, the relief centre recorded an increase in evacuees, including nine senior citizens and three people with disabilities.

Title: Firecracker materials spark blaze at Gelang Patah fruit stall [WATCH]
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: A fruit stall storing firecrackers caught fire, destroying about 60 per cent of the structure in Taman Nusa Perintis, Gelang Patah, here, last night.
The fire, which involved a temporary structure measuring 20 by 50 square feet, caused no injuries or casualties.
The Johor Fire and Rescue Department operations centre said it received an emergency call at 9.20pm.
It said a team of seven personnel, led by Senior Fire Officer I Saifulizam Salleh from the Iskandar Puteri Fire and Rescue Station, rushed to the scene with a fire engine and arrived six minutes later.
"Upon arrival at the scene, the operations team found a fire outside a fruit stall storing firecrackers.
"The team carried out extinguishing operations using two 61-metre hose reels with water sourced from a fire hydrant," the statement said.
The fire was brought under control, and extinguishing and overhaul operations ended at 10.52pm.
Earlier, a 32-second video went viral on social media showing the stall on fire and sparks from fireworks shooting off outside the premises.

Title: Grieving Spain demands answers for latest rail disaster
Article:
TOLEDO: Spain began demanding answers on Thursday after its second high-speed train collision this year killed 69 people and injured scores, as distraught relatives desperately sought news about their loved ones.
One of Europe's deadliest rail disasters this century struck south of Madrid on Wednesday morning when a service operated by state operator Renfe ploughed into the back of a stationary train belonging to private Spanish company Iryo.
Manuel San Emeterio, whose 54-year-old brother Pepe is missing, travelled to the central city of Toledo to provide DNA samples to the Civil Guard.
"The uncertainty is the worst thing that you deal with, everyone is dealing with it," he said. "But I think there's something that counters it, which is hope... we must never lose it."
Toledo has received 52 of the bodies, overwhelming its morgue's capacity of 30 and forcing the army to set up an improvised facility.
Forensics experts in green jackets, a black funeral car and army vehicles moved in and out of the site, equipped with red marquees and refrigerated containers, an AFP reporter saw.
Sniffer dogs and thermal drones were searching for bodies at the crash site outside the central village of Urda, about 130km south of Madrid.
The death toll rose from 68 to 69 on Thursday, according to regional authorities. Among the victims was Fatima Banez, a former labour minister for the main conservative Popular Party (PP).
[[nid:1566665]]
'Nervous and desperate' relatives
Jose Miguel Fernandez, a parish priest in Urda, joined emergency services in offering support to families still waiting to learn the fate of their loved ones.
"Many of them were calm, others were nervous and desperate. They wanted to know straight away and get news" of their loved ones, he told AFP.
Flags flew at half-mast on public buildings, while official ceremonies and public events were cancelled or scaled back on the first of three days of national mourning.
A minute's silence was observed across the country, including at Spain's busiest train station, Atocha in Madrid, where some mourners shed tears.
Wednesday's accident happened on a key line linking Madrid to the southern city of Seville, which was also the scene of a collision in January that killed 46 people.
It has raised fresh questions about safety on Spain's high-speed rail network, the second-largest in the world after China's.
Toledo resident Marcos Ibanez, who works in tourism, told AFP he had avoided high-speed trains "for a long time because of this".
"I've gone through the place where the accident happened several times... and you never know when it might be your turn," the 28-year-old said. "Most people are pretty fed up."
During a visit to the disaster site, Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, who faces a general election on Nov 29, pledged "to establish every last detail of this tragedy and strengthen safety measures to ensure it never happens again".
King Felipe VI also intervened in the debate after visiting the injured in Toledo, calling for measures "to ensure this does not happen again".
[[nid:1566664]]
'Searching for culprits'
Transport Minister Oscar Puente said on Wednesday that an automatic control system had gone down along 69km of track, causing all trains there to be stopped.
But the control centre decided to "resume traffic in circumstances that, from our point of view, are inexplicable", Puente said, with the Renfe train travelling 25km before striking the Iryo.
The control centre "had more than enough time to verify the error, and they did not fix it", he added.
Sanchez's main rival, PP leader Alberto Nunez Feijoo, accused Puente of "frivolity" by trying to pin the blame on one control centre operator.
"Political responsibilities cannot wait for an investigation," Feijoo said.
The head of train driver union Semaf, Diego Martin, said "attention is wrongly being focused on searching for culprits" when workers were using "degraded systems".
Renfe train drivers on Thursday maintained a strike that Semaf had called before the accident "to defend rail safety", saying previous commitments on the issue had been broken.
Renfe reported "a major impact" on its minimum service requirements, with 26.6 per cent of the staff concerned joining the industrial action.
The Madrid region's sprawling commuter network suffered the most disruption, with 81 per cent of its planned services cancelled.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Four Melaka seats set for PH-Bersatu clashes
Article:
MELAKA: Four state constituencies will see straight or multi-cornered contests between Pakatan Harapan and Bersatu in the Melaka election following the party's announcement of eight candidates last night.
The seats are Ayer Keroh, Klebang, Gadek and Pengkalan Batu, all of which PH will be defending in the Nov 14 polls.
Bersatu secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali said the party was leaving it to Melaka voters to decide who deserved to represent them, despite the overlap in seat allocations with PH.
The party's election director said Bersatu would continue to compete without resorting to smear tactics, instead offering policies focused on public welfare, economic growth and job creation.
He said its candidates would promote the party's people-centred policies, including addressing economic concerns, driving growth and creating employment opportunities.
"I believe the people of Melaka are mature enough, having changed governments in the past.
"We hope they will once again demonstrate maturity and fairness by giving Bersatu the opportunity to represent them," he said.
He was speaking after Bersatu's candidate announcement ceremony at the party's main operations room at Baitul Tariq in Klebang last night.
On overlapping seat allocations with other parties, Azmin said the situation meant they would compete against one another in the election, describing it as part of a healthy democratic process.
"We take the stand that competition is healthy in a democratic system.
"Ultimately, let the people decide who should represent them in that area," he said.
Yesterday, six Bersatu members of parliament signed a Confidence and Supply Agreement (CSA) with the Madani government at Parliament.
Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin said the agreement included the six MPs' commitment to support Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's administration until the end of the parliamentary term, including the 2027 Budget.
The other signatories, apart from Muhyiddin, were Radzi Jidin (Putrajaya), Datuk Ali Biju (Saratok), Datuk Suhaimi Abdullah (Langkawi), Datuk Dr Nazri Abu Hassan (Merbok) and Datuk Azman Nasrudin (Padang Serai).

Title: Bank of Japan to hold rates, signal further hikes
Article:
TOKYO: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) is set to keep interest rates steady on Friday but stress its focus on preventing underlying inflation from overshooting its two per cent target, suggesting scope to raise borrowing costs as soon as December.
Such guidance would reinforce the central bank's message last month that it has entered a new, more hawkish policy phase and is open to raising rates once every few months, analysts said.
The shift would also align the BOJ with its US and European counterparts, which are eyeing near-term rate hikes to tackle inflationary risks from the artificial intelligence (AI) boom and the energy shock triggered by the Iran war.
"Global price pressures from AI investment are quite strong, which means the recent inflation is partly demand driven," said Kazuo Momma, a former BOJ executive who is currently executive economist at Mizuho Research Institute.
"By declaring that its policy phase has changed, the BOJ is essentially telling markets it will hike rates once a quarter," he said, predicting rate hikes in December and March next year.
At the two-day meeting ending on Friday, the BOJ is expected to maintain its policy rate at 1.25 per cent, foregoing a back-to-back hike to allow more time to scrutinise the impact of previous rate increases on lending conditions.
In its quarterly report, the BOJ is likely to slightly revise upwards its price forecast for the next financial year and signal that underlying inflation has roughly reached its 2 per cent target, people familiar with the matter told Reuters.
With wage gains becoming embedded and inflation expectations hovering around two per cent, the central bank is likely to stress that it will now focus on anchoring inflation around its target by raising rates towards levels deemed neutral to the economy.
Markets will scrutinise comments from Governor Kazuo Ueda's post-meeting news conference for clues on the pace and timing of further rate hikes.
"If the BOJ were to say underlying inflation reached levels consistent with its two per cent price target, that would have important policy implications," said former BOJ official Nobuyasu Atago, who is currently chief economist at Rakuten Securities Economic Research Institute.
"It would be a show of resolve the BOJ won't tolerate any further overshoot in inflation," and signal the possibility of more nimble rate hikes next year, he said.
With persistently high energy costs and rising import prices due to a weak yen adding to inflationary pressures, the BOJ raised rates in September after delivering an increase in June, a shorter interval than the roughly twice-yearly hikes in 2024 and 2025.
Most analysts polled by Reuters expect the BOJ to raise its policy rate to 1.5 per cent in December, followed by further increases next year. Their projections for the terminal rate centre around 1.75 to two per cent.
Annual core inflation in Tokyo, seen as a leading indicator of nationwide price trends, exceeded the central bank's two per cent target by a wide margin in October, data showed on Friday, highlighting mounting price pressures.
Rising prices could weigh on consumption as they prompt Japanese households, many of whom have never experienced widespread price increases in their lifetime, to seek discounts.
In its latest quarterly projections in July, the BOJ expected consumer inflation to accelerate in the coming months as firms continued to pass on rising costs.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bitcoin, cryptocurrency prices fall after Binance reports security issue
Article:
SINGAPORE: Cryptocurrency prices fell on Friday after Binance reported a potential security issue and said more than US$2.5 billion in assets had been frozen.
Bitcoin dropped to a six-week low of US$77,646, while ether fell to a two-month low of US$2,238.76.
BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, fell more than 8 per cent over the past 24 hours to US$694, according to market aggregator CoinGecko.
Binance operates a secure asset fund for users, according to its website. The reserve is held entirely in bitcoin and is intended to protect user assets in the event of security breaches.

Title: Ringgit opens higher versus US dollar for 10 consecutive days
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit open higher for 10 consecutive trading days against the US dollar on Friday, reflecting continued positive sentiment in the local currency at the start of trading.
At 8am, the ringgit edged up to 4.0570/0625 against the greenback from Friday's close of 4.0575/0620.
The currency was trading near a seven-week high, with its previous opening level of 4.0560 recorded on Sept 9, 2026.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US Dollar Index (DXY) fell 0.33 per cent to 101.854 points.
He said the decline came despite better-than-expected US gross domestic product growth in the third quarter of 2026 (3Q 2026) and a higher personal consumption expenditure (PCE) inflation rate in September.
Mohd Afzanizam said the two-year and 10-year US Treasury yields also fell by 10 and eight basis points to 4.60 per cent and 4.94 per cent, respectively.
"Hence, we believe the market is pricing in the possibility that the Federal Reserve (Fed) might change its direction on monetary policy.
"As such, the ringgit is likely to maintain its positive trend in the near term, given the limited scope for further Fed monetary tightening. The ringgit-US dollar pair could therefore hover between RM4.05 and RM4.07 today," he told Bernama.
Against other major currencies, the ringgit traded lower at the opening.
It weakened against the British pound to 5.4275/4348 from 5.4009/4069 at Thursday's close, and slipped against the euro to 4.5365/5427 from 4.5176/5226.
It also edged lower against the Japanese yen to 2.5707/5743 from 2.5685/5715 previously.
Against its Asean peers, the ringgit traded mixed.
It was little changed against the Indonesian rupiah at 223.6/224.0 from 223.7/224.0 at Thursday's close, and remained flat against the Philippine peso at 6.35/6.36.
Meanwhile, the ringgit eased against the Singapore dollar to 3.1700/1746 from 3.1665/1702 at Thursday's close, and slipped against the Thai baht to 12.0279/0513 from 12.0165/0345.

Title: [UPDATED] Anwar directs Loke, Rapid KL to resolve recurring train congestion
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed Transport Minister Anthony Loke to immediately resolve train congestion issues that disrupt the daily routines of commuters.
The prime minister's directive followed complaints by a Threads user, identified as siti.anisahj, about overcrowding at train station platforms last night.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, also instructed Rapid KL to look into the issue to ensure an immediate solution.
"This happens frequently, and it certainly disrupts the daily routines of the majority of the people.
"We must be more sensitive and take action," the Tambun member of parliament said.
The prime minister's response drew widespread public attention, garnering more than 25,000 likes, nearly 300 comments, and about 1,500 reposts.
Earlier, siti.anisahj posted several photos showing the daily congestion faced by train commuters, especially in the capital.
[[nid:1566659]]
"Assalamualaikum @anwaribrahim_my. Can we ask for a few more train coaches? It is like this every day. Driving means getting stuck in traffic, while taking the train means facing overcrowding," she said.
On Oct 12, KLIA Ekspres and KLIA Transit train services were reportedly disrupted following two cable theft cases within hours along the airport rail corridor.
The incident forced commuters to endure longer travel times and altered train schedules.
The theft involved about 180m of signalling cables across two 90m sections between the Putrajaya and Cyberjaya station and the Salak Tinggi station, near the kilometre 44 marker.
On Oct 8, the Mass Rapid Transit Kajang Line at the Bukit Bintang station experienced congestion due to a surge in passenger volume, with the situation lasting for about three hours.
The congestion also affected commuters at other train stations, including the Bangsar LRT station, where many passengers were left stranded.

Title: 'Diabolical' Halloween festivities banned in Honduran towns
Article:
TEGUCIGALPA: At least six municipalities in Honduras have banned Halloween celebrations this year on the grounds that they promote wickedness.
"Permits for events whose activities, themes or content promote or incite terror or diabolical practices" will not be issued, authorities in the town of San Juan said in a statement.
Similarly, the northwestern municipality of La Libertad justified its ban as a "rejection of symbols such as witches, ghosts and monsters linked to the occult".
Shopping centres must also "refrain from promoting and selling items" related to Halloween. Violators will be fined, it said.
While the Oct 31 holiday does not have deep roots in Honduras — which is predominantly Christian, like other Central American nations — it has gained popularity in recent years among young people.
Controversy over the holiday has even reached Congress, where opposition lawmaker Dunia Jimenez has proposed banning such celebrations at schools nationwide.
The proposed ban would restrict "costume contests, decorations and recreational activities" related to Halloween.
Jimenez told AFP that some members of the public had expressed concern about such celebrations "as they consider that they do not contribute to the spiritual, ethical and moral values that they hope to promote in their children's upbringing".
Others, however, have criticised such measures as an attack on freedom of expression.
"Halloween is not a native celebration," Naydeli Alvarado, a historian and cultural manager, told AFP.
"However, people who celebrate it privately should not be punished because it undermines the secular state and restricts the freedom of citizens."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: The business of keeping people driven
Article:
OWNING a business and working in one are two very different experiences.
An owner carries the weight of the entire operation: its survival, its reputation, its financial performance and its future. Every decision has consequences, and every setback can feel personal.
For an employee, the relationship with the business is naturally different. They may be dedicated, hardworking and passionate about their role, but the business is rarely as personal to them as it is to the person who owns it.
This difference is neither a criticism of employees nor a reason to expect them to think like owners.
It is simply a reality that effective leaders must understand. An owner has a personal investment in the outcome that an employee may never fully share.
The challenge, therefore, is to build a team that understands the bigger picture and feels sufficiently motivated to contribute to it. That is where continuous training becomes essential.
Training is often treated as something that happens when a new employee joins, when a procedure changes or when performance begins to deteriorate.
This approach is too limited. Training should be an ongoing process that keeps people sharp, confident, informed and connected to the organisation's purpose.
Businesses evolve, expectations change and standards can slip when people become comfortable with familiar routines.
A team that is not continually developed can gradually become a team that merely goes through the motions.
Employees may complete their daily tasks without questioning whether they are doing them better, faster or more effectively. They may lose sight of the standards that once made the organisation successful.
Without regular guidance and renewed expectations, complacency can quietly become part of the culture.
Owners and leaders cannot assume that the energy they bring to the business will automatically be reflected in their teams.
An owner may wake up thinking about growth, costs, competition, customer satisfaction and the next challenge.
An employee may arrive focused on the responsibilities of the day and the hours remaining before they can go home. Both perspectives are understandable, but they are not identical. Leaders must bridge that gap.
Continuous training provides an opportunity to reinforce not only skills and procedures, but also purpose.
It reminds employees why their work matters, how their individual contribution affects the wider operation and what the organisation expects from them.
When people understand the reasons behind the standards they are asked to maintain, they are more likely to take ownership of their responsibilities.
However, training should never become a series of lectures delivered from behind a desk.
Effective development requires participation, demonstration, feedback and accountability.
Leaders must communicate clearly, identify weaknesses, recognise strengths and help employees understand where improvement is needed. They must also be willing to learn themselves.
A leader who expects everyone else to improve while remaining resistant to change will struggle to inspire genuine progress.
Repetition is equally important. People forget, habits weaken and standards drift. What was understood six months ago may no longer be practised consistently today.
Revisiting expectations is not necessarily a sign that employees have failed; it is a way of keeping good habits alive.
Regular reinforcement helps turn knowledge into behaviour and behaviour into consistent performance.
Just as importantly, training creates an opportunity to identify potential. Some employees need guidance to improve their current performance, while others are ready for greater responsibility.
Without regular engagement, these differences may go unnoticed.
Developing people allows leaders to build capability within the organisation, strengthen succession and reduce dependence on a handful of individuals.
There is also a powerful message in the act of investing in people. When an organisation continually develops its team, it demonstrates that employees are worth the time and effort required to help them succeed.
This can strengthen confidence, engagement and loyalty. People are more likely to care about the quality of their work when they believe their contribution is recognised and their development matters.
Nevertheless, training alone cannot manufacture commitment. Employees also need fair treatment, clear expectations, appropriate resources and leaders who practise what they preach.
Motivation cannot be demanded every morning and then abandoned when the working day becomes difficult. It must be cultivated through consistency, communication, example and a workplace culture that rewards effort and addresses poor performance fairly.
Ultimately, business owners must recognise that their personal drive cannot be the organisation's only source of momentum.
They need systems, standards and people who can sustain performance even when the owner is not present. That requires more than hiring capable employees and hoping they will remain motivated.
It requires continuous investment in their knowledge, confidence, discipline and understanding of the business.
A business grows when its people grow with it. The responsibility of a leader is not simply to direct a team, but to keep developing it, challenging it and reminding it of what it can achieve.
Training is not an interruption to the work of running a business. It is part of the work itself.
Because the difference between a team that simply completes its duties and one that consistently delivers results often comes down to leadership: the willingness to keep teaching, keep communicating and keep the purpose alive.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Potential Maxis-U Mobile merger may squeeze earnings, dividends
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A merger between Maxis Bhd and U Mobile Sdn Bhd could weigh on both telcos in the near term, with higher 5G capital expenditure, weaker earnings and dividend pressures, said Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB).
However, HLIB said the deal could help restore market discipline by absorbing an aggressive price competitor, potentially easing price competition in a two-player market.
The telcos were reported to have revived merger talks, with U Mobile's owners now seeking a valuation of more than RM10 billion, down from RM14 billion previously.
"The lower ask falls within Maxis' earlier offer range and, in our view, raises the probability of a deal," it said.
HLIB said a combination would reduce the market from three operators to two, adding that Maxis and U Mobile will form a subscriber base broadly on par with CelcomDigi Bhd.
If the merger materialises, Maxis will gain U Mobile's nationwide 5G network, preserving network differentiation rather than converging to parity with CelcomDigi under Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB).
Maxis will need to exit DNB, leaving CelcomDigi and YTL to shoulder its cost base.
HLIB kept its "Overweight" call on the telco sector as it continues to see an attractive risk-reward profile for the fixed line operators, given their key role in broadband/5G infrastructure and data centre deployments in Malaysia.
"For mobile, we maintain our ratings on Maxis and CelcomDigi for now pending more concrete developments and management updates at their upcoming results briefings," HLIB said.
Meanwhile, Maxis shares rose in early trade following reports of renewed plans for a potential merger with U Mobile Sdn Bhd.
At 10.23am, Maxis shares rose 1.42 per cent or five sen to RM3.56, with 268,300 shares traded before settling at RM3.57 at midday.
The stock closed at RM3.54, up three sen or 0.85 per cent, with 1.89 million shares changing hands, giving the company a market capitalisation of RM27.76 billion.

Title: Govt ready to offer more incentives to steel manufacturers
Article:
PETALING JAYA: The government is prepared to offer fresh incentives to Malaysian steelmakers investing in higher-value products, including automotive-grade steel and high-tech components, as the industry faces stiff import competition and pressure to upgrade its capabilities.
Malaysia's steel industry is valued at about RM35 billion, equivalent to 1.7 per cent of gross domestic product.
Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Zin said manufacturers faced pricing pressure from imported steel, making it increasingly important to move beyond conventional products into higher-margin segments.
Sim said manufacturers seeking to produce more sophisticated steel products could receive additional support, building on existing incentives such as pioneer status and investment tax allowances.
"We are prepared to help local steel manufacturers enhance their capabilities through incentives and other forms of assistance, Some industry players have already received government incentives, including pioneer status and investment tax allowances.
"If they want to make additional investments to produce more complex products, the government is prepared to assist them through further incentives," he told reporters at the 15th Conference on the Status and Outlook of the Iron and Steel Industry here today.
Additional incentives could help reduce the cost of that transition, although manufacturers will still need to secure sufficient demand to justify the investment, he added.
The push comes as the industry grapples with structural challenges, including excess capacity and competition from imports.
The country both imports and exports substantial volumes of different steel products.
Malaysia produced 7.71 million tonnes of crude steel in 2025, down from a record 9.01 million tonnes in 2024, according to the Malaysian Steel Institute.
However, the dependence on imported flat steel is clear. In 2023, domestic production reportedly stood at 2.2 million tonnes against consumption of 3.7 million tonnes.
That means local production was equivalent to about 59 per cent of flat steel consumption, with a substantial supply gap.
The government has extended restrictions on new upstream steel capacity to address the mismatch between domestic production capacity and demand, while encouraging a shift towards higher-value products.
Import competition remains a concern.
In August, Malaysia launched an anti-dumping investigation into certain coated steel products from China, Taiwan and Vietnam following complaints from local manufacturers that low-priced imports were hurting the domestic industry.
The pressure has also prompted greater scrutiny of trade practices. Eight of Malaysia's nine existing anti-dumping measures cover iron and steel products, according to the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry.
The government's longer-term challenge is to help domestic producers compete on technology, product quality and productivity rather than price alone.
Automotive-grade steel and specialised materials for advanced manufacturing offer potential growth opportunities, but require investment in production technology, technical expertise and quality standards.
Sim said local steel industry had traditionally relied heavily on the construction sector, including residential and infrastructure development, but opportunities were emerging in the aerospace, automotive and data centre industries.
The aerospace sector, in particular, offered opportunities to manufacture high-tech steel components with higher profit margins, even at relatively low production volumes.
"Malaysia has an aerospace maintenance, repair and overhaul industry that requires various steel-based components. This creates opportunities for local manufacturers to explore low-volume products that offer high profit margins," he said.
In the automotive sector, Sim said local steel manufacturers needed to invest more in producing automotive-grade steel that met stricter safety standards.
However, efforts to replace imported steel remained constrained by pricing competition and the reluctance of some manufacturers to commit substantial investments to producing the required grades.
Sim said the government was developing a dedicated incentive mechanism to encourage vehicle manufacturers to increase their use of locally produced components, including steel.
The initiative, known as the New Customised Mechanism, is expected to be implemented next year, with Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani to announce further details in due course.
Sim said Malaysia currently imported about 60 per cent of its steel requirements, highlighting the need to strengthen domestic production capabilities and reduce reliance on imports.
He added that the growing data centre industry also presented opportunities for local steel manufacturers to supply components such as server racks and related equipment.
Some manufacturers had already begun exploring opportunities in the sector as part of efforts to diversify beyond traditional markets.
Sim said the government would continue supporting local steel manufacturers in upgrading their capabilities to produce more complex, higher-value products for high-tech industries.
