Title: [UPDATED] Crypto platform Binance confirms major hack, more than US$2.5bil frozen
Article:
NEW YORK: Cryptocurrency platform Binance said on Thursday that it had fallen victim to a major hack, resulting in the freezing of more than US$2.5 billion in an effort to prevent the assets from being stolen.
The company — the world's largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes — said it had suspended trading on certain products.
It nevertheless insisted: "User funds are completely safe."
Several experts said it appeared that a massive amount of assets had been stolen.
"It does look like a hack on Binance," said former Binance chief Changpeng Zhao, who no longer runs the group but remains a majority shareholder.
Paolo Ardoino, chief executive of Tether — a company that issues a cryptocurrency known as USDT — said his firm had frozen about US$1.6 billion "related to a potential Binance exchange hack".
Circle chief Jeremy Allaire said his company had frozen more than US$800 million in USDC.
USDT and USDC are both "stablecoins", or digital currencies whose value is linked to a traditional currency, the US dollar.
For several hours before Binance confirmed the attack, several industry observers said hackers had managed to access the platform.
Some said it could be the biggest-ever cyberattack of its kind, with a haul exceeding the US$1.5 billion stolen in February 2025 from the Bybit platform — an incident attributed to hackers affiliated with North Korea.
Bitcoin prices fell more than three per cent on the news.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Australian mushroom murderer loses appeal
Article:
MELBOURNE: Australian mushroom murderer Erin Patterson lost her bid to overturn her convictions on Friday, failing to prove that she was wrongfully jailed for killing three people with a poisoned lunch.
Patterson was found guilty last year of murdering her husband's parents and elderly aunt after deliberately lacing their beef Wellington meal with highly toxic death cap mushrooms.
But the 52-year-old maintained that her triple murder convictions were a "miscarriage of justice", urging the Court of Appeal in Victoria state to either set her free or have the case heard again.
The court said it had "dismissed" her application, finding insufficient grounds for a retrial.
It also found that Patterson's original jail sentence — which made her eligible for release after 33 years — did not reflect the gravity of her crimes.
The court ruled that Patterson's non-parole period should be set aside, meaning the 52-year-old is likely to die in prison.

Title: Penang beats 25 cities worldwide as cheapest base for digital nomads
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Penang has been named the world’s most budget-friendly city for digital nomads in an international study covering 26 cities across 15 countries.
The study by digital marketing agency Click Intelligence, published in Moneywise last month, placed Penang first with an overall score of 0.78,
Berita Harian
reported today.
Busan in South Korea came second, followed by Kuala Lumpur in third place.
Fukuoka in Japan and Seoul in South Korea ranked fourth and fifth respectively.
The other five cities in the top 10 were Tartu in Estonia, Chiang Mai in Thailand, Valencia in Spain, Osaka in Japan and Brno in the Czech Republic.
Digital nomads are professionals who are not tied to a specific location and use the internet and digital technology to work remotely while travelling.
The study estimated Penang’s monthly cost of living, including rent, at €850 (approximately RM3,860), highlighting its affordability alongside internet connectivity, safety and access to Malaysia’s DE Rantau Pass.
The DE Rantau Pass is a programme for eligible remote workers that allows them to stay in Malaysia for 12 months, with an option to renew the pass.
Language not a barrier
Click Intelligence co-founder and director James Owen said language was rarely an obstacle, as English was widely spoken throughout the island.
He also said Malaysia was generally regarded as a safe country to live in.
Penang Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai said the international recognition reflected the state’s growing appeal as a destination of choice for digital nomads and international visitors.
“Penang offers more than just an affordable cost of living.
“Its Unesco World Heritage status, rich multicultural heritage, world-class food, thriving arts and creative landscape, as well as beautiful natural attractions, make the state an appealing destination to live, work and explore,” he said.
Wong said the recognition also reinforced the state government’s efforts to strengthen the tourism and creative economy industries.
“Penang has the lifestyle, culture and opportunities that international visitors and digital nomads are looking for,” he said.

Title: Malaysia’s inflation eases to 1.8pc in September, govt monitors global cost pressures
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Malaysia’s inflation rate fell to 1.8 per cent last month from 1.9 per cent in August 2026, indicating that overall price pressures remained under control.
Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the government was nevertheless keeping a close watch on developments amid rising global fuel prices and production cost pressures, BuletinTV3 reported.
He said global crude oil prices had surged to US$116.80 (RM472.75) per barrel from US$90.90 in August, while Malaysia’s Producer Price Index (PPI) also rose to 12 per cent in September 2026 from 10.7 per cent the previous month.
In response, he said the government was taking a comprehensive approach through several key measures, including targeted subsidies to shield the public from the direct impact of higher fuel prices.
“The government is continuing the implementation of Budi Madani RON95 (BUDI95), maintaining the subsidised RON95 price at RM1.99 per litre, as well as Budi Madani Diesel (Budi Diesel) for eligible recipients.
“Since September, the monthly Budi95 quota has been increased to 300 litres, while the Budi Diesel quota for jeep and pick-up truck users has been raised to 400 litres,” he said in a written parliamentary reply published on the Parliament portal today.
He was responding to a question from Datuk Seri Panglima Dr Jeffrey G Kitingan (GRS-Keningau) on the government’s measures to address rising inflation and the impact of higher oil and goods prices following the conflict in West Asia.
Akmal Nasrullah said the government was also maintaining appropriate subsidy and control mechanisms, including the Subsidised Petroleum Control System (SKPS) and Subsidised Diesel Control System (SKDS) for sectors with a direct impact on transportation costs and the prices of goods.
He said these measures were aimed at easing cost pressures on the transport and logistics sectors, while preventing increases in global fuel prices from being passed on abruptly to domestic goods and services.
“Price and supply monitoring and controls for essential goods have also been strengthened, with continuous market price checks conducted through platforms such as PriceCatcher to identify price changes, particularly for items that have a significant impact on people’s cost of living.
“The allocation for the Jualan Rahmah Madani and Jualan Agro Madani programmes has also been increased to RM750 million in 2027, from RM630 million, with a target of 35,000 events.
“These initiatives include expanding Jualan Rahmah Madani to rural areas, low-cost housing areas and People’s Housing Projects (PPR), while Jualan Agro Madani offers fresh agricultural produce at prices up to 30 per cent lower,” he said.
Akmal Nasrullah said assistance for vulnerable groups would also continue through targeted aid such as the Rahmah Cash Contribution (STR) and Rahmah Basic Contribution (SARA), with allocations increased to RM16 billion.
He said SARA could also be used to purchase fresh and wet goods at 216 farmers’ markets or tamu under the Federal Agricultural Marketing Authority (Fama), while the network of small grocery shops participating in the scheme would be expanded.
“Targeted assistance also allows fiscal resources to be channelled to those most in need, rather than through blanket subsidies that also benefit higher-income groups.
“Strengthening the country’s economic resilience against external shocks is another initiative. This includes ensuring food and energy security, strengthening domestic supply chains, increasing productivity and production efficiency, and encouraging diversification of input sources and markets.
“These measures will enable the government to continue protecting the national economy from major impacts arising from supply disruptions or prolonged increases in global commodity prices,” he said.

Title: PKR urges Umno not to mislead public over rural road projects
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 30 — Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) has urged Umno not to mislead the public about the Ministry of Finance’s (MoF) directive to postpone the issuance of new Letters of Acceptance (SST) for rural road projects.
PKR deputy secretary-general Saifuddin Shafi Muhammad stressed that deferring the SST is not the same as cancelling rural development projects, as alleged by Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki.
“Do not conflate the deferral of the SST for rural road projects with allegations of a wholesale cancellation of road, water supply and electricity projects. If there is indeed an instruction for cancellation, produce the relevant documents and the list of the projects in question,” he said in a statement yesterday.
He was commenting on Asyraf Wajdi’s statement yesterday, in which the latter, among other things, urged the MoF to withdraw its directive to cancel rural development projects in Sabah and Sarawak.
Elaborating, Saifuddin Shafi said the MoF had also suspended approvals for using the Selected Pre-Qualified Open Tender (TTPKT) method for new projects following findings in the Auditor-General’s Report concerning procurement procedures and the governance of public funds.
“However, the people want these projects to be completed. Therefore, the MoF and the Ministry of Rural and Regional Development (KKDW) must promptly resolve the issues raised and provide certainty regarding the implementation of affected projects,” he said.
Refuting the perception that Sarawak had been sidelined, Saifuddin Shafi said that under Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s leadership, the state’s development allocation under Budget 2026 had more than doubled to RM6 billion, compared with RM2.9 billion in 2022.
On campaign ethics, he said Asyraf Wajdi’s call for Barisan Nasional (BN) campaign machinery to conduct itself responsibly during the Melaka state election should also be practised by all parties, including Umno itself.
“I certainly agree with Umno’s call for campaigns to be conducted responsibly and ethically, but spreading superficial facts is not part of that effort,” he said.
He said party leaders must ensure their campaign machinery’s speeches and actions, whether on the campaign trail or on social media, do not cross the line, adding that they should contest elections based on facts, their track records in public service and the policies they offer to the people.
The Election Commission (EC) has set November 14 as the polling day for the Melaka state election, with nomination day scheduled for Saturday (October 31) and early voting for November 10. — Bernama

Title: Azalina: Govt open to considering release of full report on Azam Baki shareholding probe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — The government is prepared to consider a recommendation to release the full report of a special committee investigating allegations concerning former Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief commissioner Tan Sri Azam Baki’s shareholding.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said disclosure would be considered if necessary and subject to appropriate deliberations,
Berita Harian
reported.
She said any decision would have to take into account existing legal provisions, particularly those concerning the protection of personal information, confidentiality of investigation documents and records of asset declarations, as well as the interests of relevant parties.
“Any announcement will be made by the Chief Secretary to the Government’s Office, as stated in its March 31 media statement, should there be any developments or official decisions concerning this matter that warrant informing the public.
“The issue of asset ownership and declarations, including Azam’s shareholdings, has been examined by the Special Investigation Committee established on February 13, while the same question was previously raised by the Honourable Member on June 25.
“The committee has completed its investigation independently, transparently and professionally, and its findings have been presented to the Cabinet,” she said in a written parliamentary reply published on the Parliament portal.
She was responding to a question from Khoo Poay Tiong (PH-Kota Melaka) on the findings of the special committee investigating allegations of Azam’s shareholding, possible action against him and whether the government was prepared to disclose the report.

Title: PKR urges Melaka voters to weigh track record, plans before casting ballots
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 30 — The 16th Melaka State Election gives voters a chance to assess each party’s track record and offers when choosing the state’s leadership, said Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) deputy communications director Jonathan Vela.
He said voters should consider how parties plan to fulfil their campaign commitments.
“Evaluate what has been achieved, what remains outstanding, and what plans are being put forward for the future of the state,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Jonathan said PKR will continue to champion justice for all, regardless of race, religion or background, through consistent action, inclusive policies and commitment to listening to the people.
“Ahead of the Melaka State Election, Pakatan Harapan’s (PH) theme ‘Melaka Rumah Kita’ reflects the aspiration to build a better future for the state through joint efforts and prioritising the people’s welfare,” he said.
He said for PKR, politics is not only about seeking a mandate but also ensuring policies and decisions bring meaningful changes to people’s lives.
He added that PKR will continue focusing on employment opportunities, income, cost of living, worker protection and family well-being through clear actions and measurable implementation.
Jonathan said PKR has implemented various initiatives through its role in government to strengthen social protection, expand economic opportunities, and enhance public well-being. — Bernama

Title: Sabah police cripple armed gang behind 17 luxury house break-ins involving RM304,500 in losses
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 30 — Sabah police have crippled an armed syndicate linked to 17 gang robbery and luxury house-breaking cases involving RM304,500 in losses across several districts since early this year, said Sabah Police Commissioner Datuk Jauteh Dikun.
He said the breakthrough was achieved through two special operations, Op Casa and Op Pintu, following the formation of a special task force in September to investigate two armed robberies reported in the state capital in August.
Six men, aged between 30 and 43 with a combined 75 criminal and drug-related records, were detained, while police have launched a manhunt for several other suspects still at large.
“Police also seized various valuables, including luxury watches, designer handbags, electronic devices, cars, fishing equipment, and a safe box.
“The syndicate targeted unoccupied luxury residences and did not hesitate to use bladed weapons to intimidate victims if anyone was inside,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Jauteh said investigation papers have been completed and all suspects are scheduled to be charged at the Kota Kinabalu Magistrate’s Court today.
They will face charges under Sections 395 and 397 of the Penal Code for armed gang robbery, and Section 457 of the same code for house-breaking.
The suspects also face charges under Sections 411 and 414 of the Penal Code for retaining and disposing of stolen property, Section 447 for criminal trespass, and Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63.
“Police remain committed to taking continuous action against any individual or group involved in criminal activities to ensure the peace and wellbeing of the community, especially in Sabah, are safeguarded,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027 passes policy stage; committee debate from Nov 2 as govt mulls tighter GLC rules, 1MDB recovery
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — The Supply (Budget) Bill 2027, which was passed at the policy stage following a two-week debate, stood out as a key development during this week’s Dewan Rakyat session as the proceedings also covered a range of other issues, including administrative governance, national development, and public welfare.
Budget 2027, tabled by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on October 9, secured the approval of the majority of Dewan Rakyat members on Thursday which allows the Bill to proceed to the committee stage, which is scheduled to take place from November 2 to November 26.
Also in the spotlight this week were government clarifications regarding national financial management, the recovery of assets linked to 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB), and the role of government-linked investment companies (GLICs) in advancing the public well-being agenda.
During the Ministers’ Question Time on Tuesday, the Prime Minister announced that the government is considering a proposed “Government-Owned Entities Bill to tighten the governance of government-linked companies (GLCs) and related agencies, while preventing financial irregularities previously seen in cases involving 1MDB, Felda, and Tabung Haji.
He said the proposal seeks to establish clearer legal provisions and regulations to ensure that every government-owned entity including its subsidiaries is subject to effective regulatory mechanisms.
Anwar also emphasised a prohibition on political interference in the selection of projects and investments by GLCs and GLICs, ensuring that decisions are made professionally, meticulously, and prudently.
“Government-linked institutions mandated to safeguard the interests of the Bumiputera and the Muslim community must set an example in the practice of good governance specifically regarding integrity, transparency, and management accountability,” he said.
Regarding the rights of Sabah and Sarawak, Anwar said the government stands by its decision to provide larger development allocations, based on the geographical and infrastructural needs of both states.
Meanwhile, the Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform), Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said, informed the Dewan Rakyat that several policy recommendations for the drafting of a Political Financing Bill will be presented to the Special Select Committee (SSC) in the near future.
She noted that this is to facilitate a review process and gather further feedback before the bill is finalised for consideration by the Cabinet.
In other developments, the Energy Commission is developing a comprehensive framework and set of guidelines concerning self-generation of electricity and the use of renewable energy for the data centre sector, according to Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Energy Transition and Water Transformation, Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof.
Issues concerning health, the environment, online safety, and the cost of living were also addressed in the Dewan Rakyat through question-and-answer sessions and during the winding-up of the 2027 Budget debate by the relevant ministers.
Minister of Health Datuk Seri Dr. Dzulkefly Ahmad announced that the ministry intends to introduce a “cottage hospital” concept in rural areas, in addition to expanding the outsourcing of hospital services across 16 areas by 2027 as part of an effort to strengthen public healthcare services.
The Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability will present a proposal to develop a drought action plan to the National Disaster Management Council, aiming to strengthen preparedness for weather-related impacts stemming from the El Niño phenomenon.
Meanwhile, the implementation of the BUDI Madani initiative is considered one of the nation’s successes in targeted subsidies designed to alleviate the cost-of-living burden on the public while curbing leakages in fuel subsidies. said Minister of Finance II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan.
“This is one of the measures we have introduced to help the people reduce their cost-of-living burden, while simultaneously increasing their disposable income,” he said during his winding-up speech on the Supply Bill 2027 (Budget 2027) at the policy stage for the Ministry of Finance.
The Dewan Rakyat session is scheduled to run for 37 days, concluding on December 8. — Bernama

Title: Bersatu confirms use of own logo in Melaka state election
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 30 — Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) will use its official party logo in the 16th Melaka State Election on November 14, said its secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali.
Mohamed Azmin, who is also the party election director, said he had sent an official letter to the Election Commission (EC) last week regarding the confirmation of the party’s logo usage in the state election.
“We will use the Bersatu logo. I have sent a letter to the Election Commission and the use of the Bersatu logo has been approved by Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin,” he said to reporters here yesterday.
He said this after officiating the Bersatu Candidate Announcement Ceremony for the Melaka State Election at the party’s main operations room in Baitul Tariq, Klebang, here last night.
Also present at the event was Bersatu vice-president Datuk Dr Mohd Radzi Md Jidin.
Commenting on the eight seats contested by Bersatu in the Melaka State Election, Mohamed Azmin said all those seats were seen as having the potential to be won by the party.
According to Mohamed Azmin, although Bersatu is expected to clash with the Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidates in the four contested seats, namely in Kelebang (PKR) as well as Gadek, Ayer Keroh and Pangkalan Batu (DAP), however, they leave it to the wisdom of the people of Melaka to make their choice.
“In the context of elections, overlap or clashes mean that the parties involved will compete, but we take the stance that this competition is a healthy competition in a democratic system.
“We will not practice ‘gutter politics’ or slander, we will offer party policies... we are a party that cares for the people, focusing on issues of the economy, growth and job creation,” he also said.
Earlier, at the event, Mohd Radzi announced that Bersatu will contest in eight State Assembly seats namely Lendu, Gadek, Sungai Udang, Pantai Kundor, Kelebang, Pengkalan Batu, Ayer Keroh and Bemban. — Bernama

Title: Perikatan delays naming candidate for one Melaka state seat, denies allocation dispute
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 30 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) has postponed announcing its candidate for one remaining state seat allocated to the coalition under an understanding with Barisan Nasional (BN) for the 16th Melaka state election.
Its chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar said the delay was due to several outstanding matters, not a lack of qualified candidates.
“We have one seat for which we have yet to announce a candidate, but this is not because we lack suitable candidates. There are matters that need to be resolved, which is why we did not announce the name tonight.
“We will settle all the seats by nomination day,” he told reporters at a press conference after PN's candidate announcement ceremony at Dewan Muallim Haji Abdul Wahid, Bukit Katil, here last night.
Asked whether the delay stemmed from disputes over seat allocations among coalition component parties, Ahmad Samsuri said this was not the case.
He also confirmed that the coalition had mutually agreed to allocate another seat, Bandar Hilir, to MCA.
“Insya-Allah, we are contesting to win. That is the most important thing, and I believe our machinery is working towards that goal. With this cooperation and understanding, I believe success is within our reach,” he said.
The Election Commission (EC) has set November 14 for polling in the Melaka state election, with nomination on October 31 and early voting on November 10. — Bernama

Title: Melaka polls: Perikatan names five candidates
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 30 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) has announced five candidates for the 16th Melaka state election next month.
The names of the candidates were announced by PN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar at Dewan Muallim Haji Abdul Wahid in Bukit Katil here last night.
PN’s candidates for the Melaka state election are as follows:
N.13 Paya Rumput - Rafie Ahmad
N.16 Ayer Keroh - Datuk Seri Michael Gan
N.17 Bukit Katil - Ridzuan Sarif
N.19 Kesidang - Albert Kok
N.24 Bemban - Dr Mohd Yadzil Yaakub
The Melaka state legislative assembly was dissolved on September 23, and the Election Commission (EC) has set November 14 as polling day, with nomination day on October 31 and early voting on November 10. — Bernama

Title: PAS’ Tuan Ibrahim claims Pakatan fears BN-Perikatan unity ahead of Melaka polls
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is deeply wary of the unity between Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) in the upcoming Melaka state election, PAS deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man claimed.
He said the cooperation could deliver a major victory for the coalition,
Sinar Harian
reported today.
“God willing, with the strength we have and the combined machinery from across the country, I would like to take this opportunity to thank the entire PN leadership and all component parties for mobilising their machinery to ensure our victory in this election,” he said.
He was speaking at PN's Melaka state election candidate announcement ceremony at Dewan Muallim Haji Abdul Wahid in Bukit Katil in Melaka on Thursday night.
Tuan Ibrahim also urged party machinery members to set aside petty issues throughout the campaigning period and not be influenced by agendas pursued by certain parties.
“We know the challenge posed by AI is enormous today. Various media will be used in all kinds of ways.
“The aim is to create doubt among party supporters, question decisions and candidates, dig up secrets and even look for things that do not exist to tarnish our candidates,” he said.
He added that all party members should accept the candidates chosen by the party, saying they were the best choices for the people.
He said every candidate had undergone a vetting process at the Syura Ulama Council level.
“PAS is well known as a party whose members are obedient and abide by the party’s decisions.
“Once the party has made a decision, whether you like it or not, you must obey and comply, as long as you are not instructed to do something sinful,” he said.

Title: One held as Kelantan police open three investigation papers over extreme social media comments
Article:
TUMPAT, Oct 30 — Police have opened three investigation papers in relation to extreme comments on social media related to enforcement issues that are alleged to threaten public order and tarnish the image of the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM).
Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said a male suspect has been detained in relation to this case, whereas two other cases are under investigation and the suspects have been identified.
He said the case is being investigated under Section 504 of the Penal Code, Section 14 of the Minor Offences Act 1955 and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
“The police have never rejected criticism or reprimands aimed at improvement and safeguarding the public’s interest.
“However, action will be taken against statements that are insulting, defamatory, or extreme accusations that can disrupt public order,” he said at a press conference after patrolling the country’s waters at the Region Three Marine Police Force jetty, Pengkalan Kubor, here yesterday.
In related developments, he said that 42 individuals were detained in Kelantan this year for offences under the Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act 2007 (ATIPSOM).
Of that number, two individuals were detained for human trafficking offences, while the 40 others were involved in migrant smuggling offences.
Mohd Yusoff said that this number of arrests was compared to 59 individuals in 2025 and 51 in 2024.
He added that the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) will continue to intensify enforcement efforts to combat the smuggling of undocumented migrants and curb the involvement of any parties in such syndicates.
Meanwhile, Mohd Yusoff said that members of the public who receive threats from the illegal immigrant smuggling syndicate in Kelantan are urged to come forward and file a police report to enable an investigation to be conducted and action to be taken against the parties involved.
He said that reporting the incident to the authorities is more effective than merely spreading information or allegations through social media, which can expose the informant to further threats.
The public need not worry too much about coming forward to assist the investigation because witness protection mechanisms are available for cases that meet the criteria, including high-profile cases.
“It is better to report to the police so that we can conduct further investigations, identify the perpetrator and take action, including making arrests to resolve the issue,” he said.
He said that community cooperation is very important in efforts to combat smuggling activities using sea routes, especially in the Malaysia-Thailand border area.
In related developments, Mohd Yusoff said that a total of 4,873 immigrants were detained by various enforcement agencies in Kelantan from January to October this year, with 3,100 of them detained in districts bordering Thailand, including Kota Bharu.
He also said that Myanmar nationals recorded the highest number of arrests, with 1,977 people, followed by Bangladeshi (899), Indonesian (740), and Thais (more than 600), while the rest involved other nationalities, making a total of 26 nationalities involved in the arrests.
Mohd Yusoff added that the number of arrests this year also exceeded the record of 4,166 people for the entire year of 2025 and 3,689 people in 2024, thus showing that enforcement actions against the entry of immigrants continue to be intensified. — Bernama

Title: Damaged concrete pipe behind Bayan Baru sinkhole, road closed for repairs until Nov 7, says Penang exco
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 30 — Damage to a 750-millimetre concrete pipe has been identified as the cause of a sinkhole on Mayang Pasir Highway in Bayan Baru near here, with repair works expected to be completed by November 7.
Penang Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said Indah Water Konsortium (IWK) Sdn Bhd was carrying out repairs in stages to ensure safety at the site.
“The sinkhole has been temporarily covered with a steel plate, and safety measures in the area have been strengthened. IWK is also diverting the water flow and pumping water out of the sinkhole in preparation for the next phase of repairs,” he said in a statement last night.
He said sheet piling works to stabilise the ground were scheduled to begin tomorrow, ahead of excavation works.
The affected road will remain closed until repairs are completed. Motorists have been advised to use alternative routes via Lebuh Mayang Pasir, Jalan Mahsuri and Lorong Mayang Pasir 1.
The sinkhole, measuring about 2.5 metres in diameter and four metres deep, was discovered on Mayang Pasir Highway yesterday and is believed to have been caused by damage to IWK’s sewerage system. — Bernama

Title: Lim Guan Eng says SMEs oppose mandatory EPF contributions for foreign workers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Bagan MP Lim Guan Eng has urged the government to exempt existing foreign workers from mandatory Employees Provident Fund (EPF) contributions and a proposed RM300 monthly minimum wage increase, saying the measures would impose additional costs on local businesses, particularly micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
The DAP lawmaker said he had told Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim that employers, including MSMEs, were opposed to the mandatory contributions and the increase in minimum wages for existing foreign workers.
He claimed Anwar had been given misleading information suggesting that employers had begun accepting the requirement for a 2 per cent EPF contribution for foreign workers.
In a written parliamentary reply on October 22, Anwar said 78,129 employers had contributed to the EPF for 1,754,460 non-Malaysian workers since the mandatory scheme was introduced in October 2025.
Of these employers, 67,194, or 86 per cent, were SMEs, which Anwar said indicated that the policy was beginning to gain acceptance and was being implemented by employers.
However, Lim said those responsible for SME affairs had failed to inform the prime minister of the actual opposition among businesses to the policy.
He said the mandatory EPF contributions should apply only to newly recruited foreign workers, as the requirement was not included in existing employment contracts.
Lim argued that imposing the contributions on existing foreign workers would increase employers’ labour costs unexpectedly and affect their financial position.
He cited the Malaysian Employers Federation’s estimate in 2025 that annual spending on foreign workers’ wages exceeded RM70 billion, saying the financial implications for the national economy could be substantial.
Lim also objected to raising the monthly minimum wage for existing foreign workers by RM300, from RM1,700 to RM2,000, saying this would have an even greater financial impact on employers and contradict existing salary agreements.
He questioned the government’s reliance on International Labour Organisation (ILO) principles against discrimination between foreign and local workers to justify extending the same benefits to foreign employees.
Lim asked why foreign domestic workers were exempt from the mandatory 2 per cent EPF contribution despite also being foreign workers.
He also cited Singapore’s decision to exclude foreign workers from contributions to its Central Provident Fund, which is similar to Malaysia’s EPF, from January 1, 2003, questioning why the ILO had taken no action over the arrangement.
On minimum wages, Lim questioned why Malaysian workers employed by companies with annual sales of less than RM50 million were not required to comply with the additional RM300 increase, while domestic workers were also exempt.
He asked whether these exemptions did not amount to discrimination.
Lim said he had conveyed the concerns and dissatisfaction of MSMEs to Anwar during a meeting at the Parliament administrative block on Tuesday, October 27.
He urged the government to prioritise local employers by exempting existing foreign workers from mandatory EPF contributions and the additional RM300 minimum wage increase.

Title: Man dies after car swept away by floodwaters in Rembau; separate rescue saves Indonesian man, says Fire Dept
Article:
SEREMBAN, Oct 30 — A 74-year-old man was killed after the Perodua Myvi he was driving was swept away by floodwaters while travelling along a road near a drain beside Sungai Kampung Kundur Hulu here in Rembau last night.
Rembau Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) senior operations commander Mohamad Khairul Yahaya said it received an emergency call from the victim’s son at 9.20pm.
“The rescue team, with assistance from the Water Rescue Team (PPDA) from the Teluk Kemang BBP, managed to extricate the victim, who was trapped inside the car, about half an hour later.
“The victim, a retired civil servant, was confirmed dead by Ministry of Health medical officers and his remains were taken to Rembau Hospital,” he told Bernama.
He said the rescue operation, which involved 13 personnel, including two senior officers from the Rembau and Teluk Kemang fire and rescue stations, ended at 10pm.
In a separate incident, Mohamad Khairul said his team rescued a 38-year-old Indonesian man who was trapped among trees after being swept away by strong currents during a flash flood at Jalan Pedas-Linggi, Kampung Kundur Tengah, Pedas, here.
He said rescuers used a human-chain technique and they brought the victim to the riverbank at 8.40pm. — Bernama

Title: Petronas’ continued role as MotoGP main sponsor up for discussion, says Zahid
Article:
BANGI, Oct 30 — The proposal to ensure that Petronas remains the main sponsor of MotoGP in the coming years will be discussed with the president and Group chief executive officer of Petronas, Tan Sri Tengku Muhammad Taufik Tengku Aziz.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said this after his meeting with MotoGP executive director Carmelo Ezpeleta, who expressed hope that Petronas would continue its involvement in the prestigious international motorcycle racing championship.
“I met Carmelo, and he offered Petronas the opportunity to continue as a sponsor of MotoGP. He told me this would be Petronas’ final year as an organiser; but in other countries, their national oil companies or local companies serve as sponsors.
“He wants Malaysia’s name to be synonymous with Petronas and MotoGP. I will meet Tan Sri Taufik to discuss this matter,” he said.
He told reporters this after attending the AZH Club-organised MotoGP Casual Chat Session, which brought together more than 3,000 motorsports fans.
Ahmad Zahid said that although sponsorship costs might be high, several alternative approaches could be explored to ensure Petronas remains MotoGP’s main organiser and sponsor in the coming years.
“Although the costs may be quite substantial, I believe there are several other ways to ensure that Petronas remains the main organiser and sponsor of MotoGP,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Govt plans to reform development expenditure allocation based on states’ needs, says Economy Ministry
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — The government plans to reform federal development expenditure by moving away from a historical spending-based approach towards a model that prioritises equity and efficiency to narrow regional productivity gaps.
The Economy Ministry said the main focus was to trim the productivity gap between less-developed states and the national average.
“Annual increases in allocations under Budget 2027 do not necessarily mean that states receiving smaller allocations are underperforming compared with more developed states.
“Instead, these states may be more capable of diversifying their local economies by leveraging existing resources,” the ministry stated in a reply to the Dewan Rakyat today.
The ministry was responding to Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar (PN-Kemaman) on targets to narrow regional productivity gaps and mechanisms for allocating development funds based on the needs of states and their people.
The Economy Ministry said structural economic imbalances between states posed a threat to national competitiveness.
“If left unaddressed, regions lagging in production capacity will continue to widen the country’s productivity gap.
“Therefore, federal development allocations must serve as a key fiscal stimulus to address infrastructure deficits, technology gaps and labour market weaknesses in less-developed states, towards sustainable regional economic convergence,” it said. — Bernama

Title: Anwar tells Transport Ministry, Rapid KL to act on train overcrowding complaints
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed Transport Minister Anthony Loke to urgently address overcrowding on train services, warning that the problem could disrupt the daily routines of commuters.
The directive followed a complaint by a Threads user identified as siti.anisahj, who highlighted overcrowding at train stations in a post last night, according to a report by
Berita Harian
.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said he had also instructed Rapid KL to look into the problem and ensure a swift solution.
“This (train overcrowding) happens frequently and it certainly disrupts the daily routines of the wider public.
“We (the government) must be more attentive and take action,” the Tambun MP said.
The prime minister’s response attracted widespread attention, garnering more than 25,000 likes, nearly 300 comments and about 1,500 reposts.
In her earlier post, siti.anisahj shared several photographs showing the crowded conditions faced by train commuters, particularly in the capital, on a daily basis.
“Assalamualaikum @anwaribrahim_my. Could we have more train carriages, please? It's like this every day... driving means getting stuck in traffic, while taking the train means it's packed,” she wrote.
On October 12, KLIA Ekspres and KLIA Transit services were reportedly disrupted following two cable theft incidents within several hours along the airport rail corridor.
The incidents forced passengers to endure longer journeys and changes to train schedules.
The theft involved about 180 metres of signalling cables, comprising two sections of 90 metres each, between Putrajaya and Cyberjaya Station and Salak Tinggi Station, near the 44km marker.
Earlier, on October 8, the Kajang MRT Line experienced overcrowding at Bukit Bintang Station, with the situation lasting about three hours due to an increase in passenger numbers.
The congestion was also believed to have significantly affected commuters at other train stations, including Bangsar LRT Station, where many passengers were left stranded.

Title: Rural Roads Programme financing prioritised, 2026 allocation rises to RM3.1b, says Amir Hamzah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — The government is prioritising the Rural Roads Programme (JALB) project financing with the total allocation for 2026 rising to RM3.1 billion from the original allocation of RM2.11 billion, according to the Finance Ministry (MoF).
Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said the nearly RM1 billion in additional allocation comprises the additional RM500 million for the Rural and Regional Development Ministry (KKDW) and the earlier Notice of Change (NOC) worth RM491 million made by KKDW.
In his winding-up speech on the policy stage of the Supply Bill 2027 (Budget 2027), he said the additional allocation was approved to ensure that the JALB projects could continue and contractors are paid.
Amir Hamzah said the approval, granted through the Expenditure Exceeding Allocation Authorisation Letter (SKB), was issued in stages, with RM300 million approved on September 1, 2026, and RM200 million on September 21, 2026.
“This allocation was still insufficient to settle existing (KKDW) commitments,” he noted.
Amir Hamzah said the additional funds channeled through the SKB mean development expenditure savings from other ministries.
Among the ministries are the Women, Family and Community Development Ministry; Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry; Tourism, Arts and Culture Ministry; Agriculture and Food Security Ministry; Transport Ministry; Housing and Local Government Ministry; and Economy Ministry.
Amir Hamzah said the actual expenditure for JALB projects from 2018 to 2022 amounted to RM3.72 billion, while actual expenditure and allocations for the 2023-2027 period reached RM11 billion.
Meanwhile, Amir Hamzah said applications for and approvals of NOCs must be completed before any new expenditure or commitments are undertaken, while any issuance of a new letter of acceptance (SST) should also be supported by sufficient allocations.
“On this basis, MoF requested KKDW on September 10, 2026, to defer the issuance of a new SST for JALB.
“Therefore, any claim that MoF cancelled the projects is untrue. MoF only requested that KKDW defer the issuance of a new SST until the existing arrears have been settled,” Amir Hamzah said.
He added that every additional allocation for JALB through reallocation reduces the fiscal space available to fund other priorities.
He said Budget 2027 brings together the strengths of the government, investment institutions, companies, banks, employers and the public based on their respective roles, whereby the collaboration expands the country’s capability to provide jobs, facilities and economic opportunities.
He said the RM50.2 billion in additional investments detailed in Budget 2027 comprises RM25 billion from government-linked investment companies (GLICs), RM11 billion from public-private partnerships, and RM14.2 billion from federal statutory bodies and Minister of Finance Incorporated companies.
“Each component has its own funding sources, mandate and approval process,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Too many good companies stay small for too long: Anwar urges Bursa Malaysia to help more local firms become regional champions
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called on Bursa Malaysia Bhd to help more Malaysian companies grow into regional champions, saying too many promising businesses remain small for too long.
“I would like to see more mid-tier companies grow, list and become regional champions. Too many good companies stay small for too long.
“Bursa has a role in helping them take that next step. If it succeeds, we should see more Malaysian businesses grow, more good jobs created and more Malaysians holding a stake in the country’s progress,” he said in his keynote address at Bursa Malaysia’s 50th anniversary celebration yesterday.
Second Finance Minister Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan, Bursa Malaysia chairman Tan Sri Abdul Farid Alias, Bursa Malaysia chief executive officer Datuk Fad’l Mohamed and Securities Commission Malaysia chairman Datuk Mohammad Faiz Azmi were also present.
Anwar added that the growth of Malaysian businesses could create more jobs and allow more Malaysians to share in the country’s progress.
He also stressed the importance of trust and fairness in the capital market, saying companies seeking investment from Malaysians must deal with them honestly.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said Malaysia’s market would face a changing global environment shaped by geopolitical tensions, technological change and the energy transition.
“The market has been through hard years. Financial crises and the pandemic tested companies, investors and regulators alike. Through each of them, the capital market kept doing its job. It kept investment flowing and helped the economy recover,” he added.
Anwar also urged Malaysian companies to move up the value chain in areas including semiconductors, advanced manufacturing and digital technology to compete confidently abroad.
The Prime Minister said the government had also put a great deal of effort into governance and fiscal discipline, as well as making Malaysia a more attractive place to invest.
“The results are showing. In the first half of this year, Malaysia recorded RM218.5 billion in approved investments. Under the Madani Economy, we are aiming to raise the ceiling of what our economy can achieve while raising the floor of our people’s living standards,” Anwar said. — Bernama

Title: ‘Which is more nerve-racking?’ Tengku Zafrul jokes about Syed Saddiq’s MoU signing with govt, wedding vows with Bella
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) chairman Datuk Seri Tengku Zafrul Abdul Aziz has poked fun at Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman, asking whether he was more nervous about exchanging wedding vows with actress Bella Astillah or signing a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the government.
In an Instagram post yesterday, Tengku Zafrul said he had posed the question to Syed Saddiq, drawing a humorous comparison between the two commitments.
“One is a promise to build a future together with a partner, while the other is a commitment to the future of Muar residents,” he wrote.
The post followed the Madani government’s signing of an MoU with Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) and several other opposition MPs, including Syed Saddiq.
Tengku Zafrul, who is also Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s senior political adviser, said the MPs would remain in the opposition despite agreeing to support the Budget and key institutional reforms.
He added that their respective constituencies would receive equivalent allocations for the benefit of the people.
“In politics, we do not necessarily have to agree on everything. But when it comes to the interests of the people, we must be able to work together,” he said.
The post was accompanied by the hashtags #TZA and #MadaniBekerja.

Title: Differing views among ministries part of healthy policy process, not disunity, says Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Differing views or approaches among ministries do not necessarily reflect division within the government, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Instead, Anwar described such differences as part of healthy policy deliberations and discussions that take into account respective responsibilities, jurisdictions, and priorities to ensure the effective implementation of the Madani Government’s agenda.
He said the government systematically coordinates between ministries to align policies, prevent overlapping functions, and ensure every decision is made based on public interest, national development priorities, and the government’s financial capacity.
“To ensure effective governance, every government policy and decision must undergo proper deliberation and coordination.
“Matters requiring a collective decision will be tabled for Cabinet consideration and approval, in line with the principle of collective ministerial responsibility,” said Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister.
He said this in a written reply published on the Parliament website yesterday in response to a question from Opposition Leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin (PN-Larut).
Hamzah had asked about recent instances where the Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Rural and Regional Development publicly issued conflicting positions on several issues.
Anwar gave an assurance that the government will continue to strengthen inter-ministerial cooperation, enhance policy implementation, and monitor initiative outcomes to ensure decisions translate into tangible and sustainable benefits for the people.
The Prime Minister added that the country’s economic performance is monitored continuously based on current indicators to assess policy effectiveness and strengthen economic resilience against global uncertainties. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027: How much could pet owners save under the new pet tax relief?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Pet owners could soon claim tax relief on adoption, vaccination and sterilisation expenses under a proposal announced in Budget 2027.
The move is aimed at helping pet owners offset some of the costs associated with caring for animals, from routine vaccinations to one-off expenses such as adoption and sterilisation.
Pet ownership costs have gradually risen over the years and, for some households, have become a growing part of monthly spending.
Instead of creating a separate allowance, the proposed relief would fall under the existing RM2,500 lifestyle tax relief limit.
The actual tax savings would depend on eligible spending, the taxpayer's applicable income tax rate and how much of the relief limit remains unused.
What pet owners are paying
Published fees from animal welfare organisations and veterinary providers offer an indication of what pet owners might pay.
Costs vary according to the animal, type of vaccine, size, sex and services included.
All figures are illustrative examples from selected published price lists, not standard rates or national averages.
Actual fees may vary by provider, location, animal and services required.
Adoption fees may include vaccination and sterilisation, so pet owners should avoid counting included services again as separate expenses.
As a pet owner, Diyana Malek said that unless her cat falls sick, she hardly spends anything on it apart from food and supplements.
“Even tick or flea medication could cost hundreds, depending on the size of the cat or dog. The prices of this medication vary.
“I send my cat to the veterinary clinic for showers. The price for that follows the weight of the cat and that starts from RM80.
“So this tax relief helps, it takes off a reasonable load,” Diyana said when contacted by Malay Mail.
The price of an average tick/flea medication ranges from RM60 to RM92, depending on the brand.
How much could pet owners save?
Using published prices as an illustration, a household with two cats and one dog could incur the following costs for vaccination and sterilisation.
If the full RM570 qualified for tax relief, the potential tax savings would depend on the taxpayer’s applicable marginal tax rate:

These are illustrative estimates, not guaranteed savings. The actual benefit would depend on the taxpayer’s chargeable income, applicable tax rate, eligible expenses and how much of the RM2,500 lifestyle relief limit remains unused.
The calculation also assumes the household pays the listed fees separately.
It does not include adoption costs or account for any vaccination or sterilisation services already covered by an adoption fee.
What pet owners should know
The proposed relief would be included within the existing RM2,500 lifestyle tax relief limit, which also covers other eligible expenses.

This means taxpayers who have already used the full limit may not receive additional relief from their pet-related expenses.
The proposal covers eligible vaccination and sterilisation services provided by registered veterinary services, as well as the cost of adopting a rescued pet from a registered animal shelter.
Since the detailed eligibility conditions and documentation requirements have yet to be announced, pet owners should check their claims against the final rules before submitting them.

Title: Johor DOE probes Sungai Kim Kim after river turns white again, cable excavation suspected
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 29 — The Johor Department of Environment (DOE) is investigating allegations that Sungai Kim Kim in Pasir Gudang has become polluted again, turning white yesterday.
Johor DOE director Dr Mohd Famey Yusoff said enforcement officers inspected the site at about 6pm following a complaint about the incident.
However, he said preliminary inspections yesterday found that the river water had returned to normal and was no longer visibly white.
Mohd Famey said preliminary investigations suggested that the incident could have been caused by a one-off waste discharge into the river.
“Nevertheless, the DOE, together with the Pasir Gudang City Council (MBPG), will examine closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage in the vicinity of the suspected dumping site,” he told Bernama.
Mohd Famey said the CCTV footage would be examined to identify the source of the pollution and those responsible.
He said strict legal action would be taken against any party or individual found to be involved in the waste dumping incident.
Yesterday, a social media post went viral alleging that Sungai Kim Kim had been polluted again, accompanied by several photographs showing the river water turning white.
The chemical pollution incident at Sungai Kim Kim in March 2019 shocked the nation, affecting more than 2,000 people and resulting in the closure of 111 schools in Pasir Gudang.
Meanwhile, State Health and Environment Committee chairman Ling Tian Soon said that the pollution was believed to have been caused by excavation work to a depth of about five metres for cable installation.
He said the information was based on further investigations conducted by the DOE today.
“The cable installation work was carried out yesterday at about 3pm,” he said in a Facebook post today.
Ling said the state government understood the public’s concerns and stressed that it took all reports involving environmental quality seriously, adding that it would ensure the relevant agencies carried out appropriate monitoring and follow-up action.
Members of the public are also encouraged to lodge complaints if they detect any suspicious activities or signs of environmental pollution, so that investigations and further action can be carried out promptly. — Bernama

Title: Govt increases allocations to all states, Sabah and Sarawak receive highest sums, says Amir Hamzah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The federal government has always prioritised projects proposed by the state governments, including increasing allocations to all states, said Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan.
He said that since 2023, several main grants have been enhanced, with the Economic, Infrastructure and Welfare Development-Based Grants (TAHAP Grants) increased to RM400 million per year.
Meanwhile, the allocation for the Malaysian Road Records Information System (MARRIS) increased to RM5.6 billion in 2026 from RM5.2 billion in 2023.
“The allocation for the Ecological Fiscal Transfer (EFT) increased to RM270 million in the 2027 Budget from RM150 million in 2023. This increase supports services, infrastructure, and environmental preservation in the states,” he said when winding up the debate on the Supply Bill 2027 at the policy stage for the Ministry of Finance (MoF) in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He said the Madani government also increased Sabah’s interim special grant from RM26.7 million in 2021 to RM1.5 billion, which is more than 50 times. For Sarawak, the interim special grant increased from RM16 million in 2022 to RM1.5 billion, which is more than 90 times.
Meanwhile, Amir Hamzah said the overall allocation for Sabah and Sarawak is the highest, increasing to RM18.7 billion and RM16.2 billion, respectively.
Sabah’s RM18.7 billion allocation comprises RM8.9 billion for operating expenses, RM7 billion for development, and RM2.8 billion in grants to the state government.
He said the government respects the principle of special grants in line with the Constitution, and negotiations are ongoing to finalise a fair and sustainable method of calculation.
“This is the commitment of the Madani Government to drive the development of Sabah and Sarawak while negotiations are underway,” he said.
Federal expenditures are projected to rise from a revised estimate of RM444.1 billion in 2026 to RM459.8 billion in 2027, of which RM376.8 billion will be operating expenditure and RM83 billion as development expenditure. — Bernama

Title: MCA gets Bandar Hilir as third Melaka seat to contest, says Wee Ka Siong
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — MCA president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong said the party has been given an additional seat - Bandar Hilir - to contest in the Melaka State Election.
He said Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) finalised the decision today, with MCA set to contest in three state constituencies, including Machap Jaya and Kelebang.
Wee said its candidate for the Bandar Hilir state seat will be Melaka Historic City Council councillor Jasmine Lok Huey Yee, 38.
“Officially, MCA will contest the two seats that we won in 2021, namely Machap Jaya and Kelebang, and now we have been given an additional seat in Bandar Hilir.
“BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi handed over the letters of appointment for candidates at 4pm today,” he told a media conference at the Parliament Building today.
Wee said the additional seat was part of the process of finalising seat allocations between BN and PN for the Melaka polls.
He said this follows key PN leaders’ willingness to allocate the seat in question to MCA, which had contested the constituency previously, adding that the move would not affect the strategic cooperation between BN and its strategic partners for the state election.
“... (we) received a call from key PN leaders expressing their willingness to allow MCA to contest, as this is a seat we had contested in the past,” he said.
Overall, BN will contest 22 seats at the 16th Melaka polls.
The Election Commission (EC) has set November 14 as the polling day for the Melaka state election, with nomination day scheduled for Saturday (October 31) and early voting for November 10. — Bernama

Title: MACC issues asset declaration notices to businessman Nazir Hussin and brother
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) issued asset declaration notices to businessman Datuk Seri Nazir Hussin Akhtar Hussin and his brother, Datuk Mubarak Hussain, on October 20.
Nazir Hussin was at the MACC Office in Putrajaya to receive the notice under Section 36(1)(a) of the MACC Act 2009, while Mubarak Hussain received the notice at his residence.
When contacted, MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the matter, saying both individuals complied with the notices.
On October 14, the MACC summoned Nazir Hussin, his wife and an aide to assist in an investigation into alleged misappropriation and abuse of position involving an investment deal worth about RM10 million.
The MACC said it summoned the former Yayasan Bank Rakyat (YBR) chairman to receive a notice requiring him to declare his assets, while his wife and the aide were summoned to record their statements.
Abd Halim was reported to have said that Nazir Hussin refused to accept the notice, citing an injunction application he had filed at the Kuala Lumpur High Court yesterday to stop enforcement of the directive issued under Section 36 of the Act. — Bernama

Title: Finance minister II: GST not an option amid high cost of living, govt sticking with SST
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The federal government will continue to implement the Sales and Service Tax (SST), as the Goods and Services Tax (GST) will not be considered due to the ongoing burden of the cost of living.
Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said the government would continue to improve the SST to reduce the impact of cascading taxes and simplify compliance.
He said the SST also provided room for a more progressive and targeted approach.
“The government can choose which goods and services to tax while exempting essential items. Although some of the tax may be passed on through prices, the scope of taxation can be determined with the people’s affordability in mind,” said Amir Hamzah during the Supply Bill (Budget 2027) policy-level winding-up debate for the Ministry of Finance (MoF) in Parliament today.
He explained that the GST tended to be regressive because lower-income groups spent a larger proportion of their income on goods and services.
“In other words, even at the same tax rate, the burden relative to income is heavier for the people, particularly the B40 and M40 groups.
“Therefore, any additional revenue must be assessed alongside the burden borne by the people,” he said.
According to the Fiscal Outlook 2027, SST collections are estimated to rise to RM67 billion in 2026 from RM55.9 billion in 2025. They are projected to reach RM73.3 billion in 2027, an increase of RM17.4 billion over two years.
Amir Hamzah said SST collections currently account for three per cent of gross domestic product (GDP), the same level recorded by the GST in 2017.
This means replacing the SST with the GST would not necessarily generate additional revenue, but would instead shift the tax burden entirely from businesses, including exporters, to the people, he emphasised.
“This increase demonstrates the SST’s ability to generate revenue to finance the country’s needs.
“At the same time, the government has the flexibility to determine which goods and services are taxed on a targeted basis while exempting essential items,” said Amir Hamzah.
He said the government recognised GST’s advantages in collection efficiency, transparency and the input tax credit mechanism. However, the choice of tax system must take into account the people’s ability to pay.
On compliance, he said nearly 700,000 businesses were registered under the GST in 2018, compared with only about 130,000 under the SST in 2026. This means more businesses would have to bear compliance costs under the GST system, said Amir Hamzah. — Bernama

Title: MOH to conduct special recruitment for 750 permanent medical officer posts in Sabah, Sarawak
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 29 — The Health Ministry (MOH) will conduct a special recruitment exercise to fill 750 permanent Medical Officer Grade UD10 vacancies in Sabah and Sarawak, with applications open from November 9 to 15.
MOH said the recruitment is open to all contract-appointed medical officers who began their housemanship training from Series 1/2016 on December 5, 2016, to Series 6/2024 on October 14, 2024, including those whose service contracts had expired.
“To be eligible, candidates must have successfully completed their housemanship training and obtained full registration with the Malaysian Medical Council by the closing date of the application advertisement at the latest,” MOH said in a statement today.
The ministry said eligible and interested officers could submit their applications through the Public Service Commission’s SPA9 system when the recruitment advertisement opened.
“For officers who are successful in securing permanent appointments, the proposed reporting date is February 15, 2027,” the statement said.
The ministry said the recruitment exercise was part of the Madani Government’s commitment to making permanent appointments for more than 9,000 medical officers, as announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim when tabling Budget 2027.
“This proactive measure is also designed to narrow the staffing gap and ensure that the retention of the medical workforce in Sabah and Sarawak remains at an optimal level,” the statement said. — Bernama

Title: Former Pahang water firm procurement manager begins three-year jail term after losing bribery appeal
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 29 — The Court of Appeal today upheld the three-year jail sentence and RM239,500 fine imposed on a former procurement manager of Pengurusan Air Pahang Berhad after dismissing his appeal to set aside his conviction on 22 charges of receiving RM44,700 in bribes.
A three-member panel led by Justice Datuk Noorin Badaruddin ruled that Sani Khan Ali Khan had failed to show any error of law or material fact in the High Court decision that convicted him on all the charges.
On January 26, the Kuantan High Court set aside a Sessions Court decision that had acquitted and discharged him of all the charges.
The Court of Appeal panel, which also comprised Justices Datuk Mohd Radzi Abdul Hamid and Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid, ordered him to begin serving his sentence today.
Sani Khan, 51, had previously been granted a stay of execution and released on RM20,000 bail with one surety pending the outcome of this appeal.
In today’s proceedings, Justice Noorin said the High Court’s intervention was justified and that it had made no material error in setting aside the Sessions Court decision that had acquitted and discharged Sani Khan.
“The statutory presumption under Section 50(1) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009 applies,” she said.
She said banking records proved that the money had been received into the appellant’s bank account, and that his claim that the payments were house rental was unconvincing.
Justice Noorin said that although the appellant relied on tenancy agreements and bank transactions labelled as house rent, the court found that the documents did not prove the payments were genuine rent.
She added that the appellant had also failed to show that the alleged defects in the charges had caused him to misunderstand the case or suffer material prejudice in preparing his defence.
Justice Noorin said the evidence was assessed cumulatively, with the banking records, witness testimony, tenancy documents and surrounding circumstances weighed together for each charge. The court found no material error warranting the overturning of any of the 22 convictions.
On December 26, 2024, the Sessions Court ruled that the prosecution had failed to prove its case beyond a reasonable doubt, and acquitted and discharged Sani Khan on all the charges.
However, the High Court allowed the prosecution’s appeal to set aside his acquittal and found him guilty on all 22 charges.
The High Court imposed three years’ jail for each charge and ordered Sani Khan to pay a RM239,500 fine, or 12 months’ jail in default. The sentences were ordered to run concurrently.
At the Court of Appeal today, MACC deputy public prosecutors Law Chin How, Haresh Prakash Somiah and Hazel Tan Jia Qi appeared for the prosecution.
Sani Khan was represented by lawyers Mohd Baharuddin Ahmad Kassim, Datuk Mohd Najid Husain and Nornajihah Ahmad Nadjemudin. — Bernama
